title: Windows 11 Laptop Stuck at Manufacturer Logo on Boot
content:
Problem: A Windows laptop powers on but does not progress past the manufacturer splash screen (e.g., Dell, HP, Lenovo logo) into Windows.

Symptoms:
- Laptop powers on, fans spin, but screen stays on the manufacturer logo indefinitely
- No spinning dots or loading indicator appears
- User reports 'my laptop won't start Windows' or 'stuck on the logo screen'
- Laptop was working normally before last shutdown or update

Resolution Steps:
1. Perform a hard reset: hold the power button for 15-20 seconds until the laptop fully powers off, then power back on.
2. If it hangs again, force shutdown 2-3 more times during boot to trigger Windows Automatic Repair / WinRE.
3. In the recovery environment, choose Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Startup Repair.
4. Disconnect all external peripherals, docking stations, and USB drives, then attempt to boot again.
5. Boot into Safe Mode from the recovery menu to check if the issue is driver-related.
6. If Startup Repair fails, check System Restore to roll back to a point before the issue started.
7. Note exact laptop model, asset tag, and how many boot attempts were made before escalating to L2 for BIOS/firmware or hardware diagnostics.

Edge Case: If the logo screen shows a spinning wheel that eventually leads to a black screen with only a cursor, treat this as a separate 'black screen after boot' scenario, not a logo hang.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Startup

title: Windows Stuck in Automatic Repair Loop
content:
Problem: After a failed boot, Windows repeatedly enters 'Preparing Automatic Repair' / 'Diagnosing your PC' and then restarts into the same screen without ever reaching the desktop.

Symptoms:
- Screen shows 'Automatic Repair' or 'Diagnosing your PC' followed by an unexpected restart
- Cycle repeats indefinitely, sometimes ending in 'Automatic Repair couldn't repair your PC'
- User states 'my computer keeps restarting and repairing itself' or 'stuck in a repair loop'
- Often follows a sudden power loss, forced shutdown, or interrupted update

Resolution Steps:
1. Let the repair loop run once fully rather than interrupting it mid-cycle.
2. When the 'Automatic Repair couldn't repair your PC' screen appears, select Advanced Options.
3. Try System Restore to a restore point prior to the failure, if available.
4. Open Command Prompt from Advanced Options and run: chkdsk C: /f /r, then reboot.
5. If disk check does not resolve it, run: sfc /scannow followed by DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth from the recovery Command Prompt.
6. As a last resort before escalation, offer 'Reset this PC' with the 'Keep my files' option.
7. If none of the above succeed, escalate to L2 for image reimaging, noting whether user data has been backed up.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Startup

title: Laptop Powers On But Screen Stays Black
content:
Problem: Laptop appears to power on (fans running, power light on, keyboard backlight active) but the display never shows anything — not even the manufacturer logo.

Symptoms:
- Power LED is on and fans/hard drive can be heard, but screen remains completely black
- No BIOS/manufacturer logo, no cursor, no backlight change on the panel
- User reports 'blank screen', 'black screen on startup', or 'nothing shows on the display'
- External monitor may or may not show output when connected

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the laptop is actually powered on by listening for fan noise and checking keyboard backlight or caps lock light response.
2. Adjust screen brightness using the function key combination in case brightness was set to zero.
3. Connect an external monitor via HDMI/USB-C to determine if the issue is the internal panel or the GPU/motherboard.
4. Perform a hard reset by holding the power button 15-20 seconds, then power back on.
5. Remove any external displays, docks, or peripherals and attempt to boot with a minimal configuration.
6. Listen for POST beep codes if available and note them for escalation.
7. If an external monitor also shows nothing, escalate to L2/hardware team as a likely motherboard, RAM, or power issue; if external monitor works but internal panel does not, log as a display/panel hardware fault.

Edge Case: If the screen briefly flashes the logo then goes black, this is different from a true no-output black screen and should be treated as a startup/boot hang rather than a display hardware fault.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, all laptop hardware
Category: Windows / Startup

title: Windows Update Stuck Downloading or Installing
content:
Problem: Windows Update remains stuck at a percentage (e.g., 'Downloading update 45%' or 'Working on updates 30% complete') for an extended period without progressing.

Symptoms:
- Progress bar or percentage in Settings > Windows Update does not move for 30+ minutes
- User reports 'update is frozen', 'stuck downloading updates', or 'stuck at X percent'
- Windows Update troubleshooter may report no issues found
- System may feel sluggish while the update service consumes CPU or disk resources

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm there is adequate free disk space (at least 20 GB recommended) using File Explorer or 'This PC'.
2. Run the built-in Windows Update Troubleshooter from Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters.
3. Restart the laptop once, since some updates require a restart to continue progressing rather than being truly stuck.
4. If still stuck after restart, stop the Windows Update service (wuauserv) via services.msc, rename the C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution folder, and restart the service.
5. Re-check for updates in Settings > Windows Update after clearing the SoftwareDistribution cache.
6. Ensure the laptop remains plugged into power and connected to Wi-Fi/Ethernet throughout the update.
7. If the update fails again with the same behavior, escalate to L2 with the update KB number from Update History.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Update

title: Windows Update Fails With Error 0x80070070 (Low Disk Space)
content:
Problem: A Windows Update installation fails with error code 0x80070070, indicating there is not enough free disk space to complete the update.

Symptoms:
- Windows Update history shows 'Failed - 0x80070070'
- Message may read 'There's not enough space on your PC'
- User reports the update repeatedly fails at the same step
- C: drive shows low remaining free space in File Explorer

Resolution Steps:
1. Check available free space on the system drive via File Explorer; aim for at least 15-20 GB free.
2. Run Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe) and select 'Clean up system files' to remove old update files and temporary data.
3. Empty the Recycle Bin and clear the Downloads folder of large unneeded files with user permission.
4. Use Storage Sense (Settings > System > Storage) to automatically free up space.
5. If space is still limited, ask the user to move large personal files (videos, ISOs) to OneDrive or an external drive.
6. Re-run Windows Update once sufficient space is confirmed.
7. If the error persists despite adequate free space, escalate to L2 to check disk health and update component corruption.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Update

title: Laptop Restarts Repeatedly After Windows Update Installation
content:
Problem: After a Windows Update installs, the laptop enters a cycle of restarting repeatedly ('Restarting' or 'Working on updates, don't turn off your computer') without ever completing setup.

Symptoms:
- Laptop restarts multiple times in a row after an update, never reaching the desktop
- Screen shows 'Restarting' or a percentage that resets after each reboot
- User reports 'my laptop won't stop restarting after the update'
- May eventually show 'Undoing changes made to your computer' as Windows attempts rollback

Resolution Steps:
1. Allow the restart cycle to complete at least 2-3 times, since Windows may self-correct and roll back the failed update automatically.
2. If it does not resolve, force a shutdown by holding the power button, then boot into Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) by interrupting boot 2-3 times.
3. From WinRE, go to Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Uninstall Updates and remove the most recent quality or feature update.
4. After uninstalling the problematic update, boot normally and confirm the laptop stabilizes.
5. Pause updates for 7 days via Settings > Windows Update while the issue is investigated.
6. Check Update History once stable to identify the specific KB article number that caused the loop.
7. Escalate to L2 with the KB number so the update can be flagged before wider deployment.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Update

title: User Locked Out After Forgetting Local Windows Password
content:
Problem: A user cannot sign in to their Windows laptop because they have forgotten their local (non-domain, non-Microsoft account) password.

Symptoms:
- User reports 'I forgot my computer password' or 'I can't log into my laptop'
- 'The password is incorrect' message appears repeatedly at the lock screen
- No Microsoft account or Entra ID/Azure AD is associated with the login
- User cannot use 'Forgot password' link because the account is local only

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm whether the device is domain-joined/Entra ID joined or a local-only account; if managed, use the standard enterprise password reset process instead.
2. For local accounts, check if a password reset disk was previously created; if so, use it at the login screen.
3. If the account is an administrator-created local account, have another local admin on the device reset the password via Control Panel > User Accounts.
4. If no other admin account exists, boot into Safe Mode (if the built-in Administrator account is enabled) to reset the password.
5. As a last resort for company-owned devices, escalate to L2 for a supported password reset or account recovery procedure per company policy.
6. Verify the user's identity per security policy before performing any reset.
7. After reset, have the user immediately change the password and confirm they can sign in.

Edge Case: Never attempt third-party password-cracking tools; only use supported Windows recovery and company-approved reset procedures.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Login

title: Windows Sign-In Screen Freezes or Goes Black After Entering Password
content:
Problem: After a user enters their correct password at the Windows lock/login screen, the screen freezes, goes black, or shows only a cursor and never reaches the desktop.

Symptoms:
- Screen turns black or shows only a mouse cursor after password entry
- No error message is displayed; the system appears hung
- User reports 'my laptop won't finish logging in' or 'stuck on a black screen after I type my password'
- May resolve temporarily after waiting several minutes, or may hang indefinitely

Resolution Steps:
1. Wait 2-3 minutes in case the desktop is simply loading slowly, particularly after an update or profile sync.
2. Try pressing Ctrl+Alt+Del and selecting Task Manager (or Sign out) to see if the system responds at all.
3. If unresponsive, perform a hard reset and attempt to log in again.
4. Attempt to sign in with Safe Mode to determine if a startup application or driver is causing the hang.
5. If Safe Mode login succeeds, disable non-essential startup apps via Task Manager > Startup and try a normal boot again.
6. Check for a corrupted user profile by attempting login with another account, if available, to isolate the issue.
7. If the issue is isolated to one profile, escalate to L2 for profile repair; if it affects all users on the device, escalate for a system-level investigation.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Login

title: 'Your Account Has Been Disabled' Message at Windows Sign-In
content:
Problem: A user attempting to log into their Windows device receives a message stating their account has been disabled, preventing sign-in.

Symptoms:
- Login screen displays 'Your account has been disabled. Please see your system administrator.'
- User was previously able to log in normally
- May follow an offboarding action, security incident, or policy enforcement in Active Directory/Entra ID
- User cannot access the device at all, even after a restart

Resolution Steps:
1. Verify with HR/IT security whether the account was intentionally disabled (e.g., offboarding, suspected compromise, policy violation).
2. Check Active Directory Users and Computers or Entra ID admin center to confirm the account's disabled status.
3. If disabled in error, re-enable the account and have the user attempt sign-in again after a few minutes for replication.
4. If the account was legitimately disabled, do not re-enable without manager or security team approval; direct the user to their manager.
5. For domain-joined devices, confirm the device itself has connectivity to a domain controller, as stale cached credentials can sometimes show similar messages.
6. Document the reason for the disablement or re-enablement in the ticket for audit purposes.
7. Escalate to the security or identity team if the disablement reason is unclear or disputed.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, Active Directory, Entra ID
Category: Windows / Login

title: Windows Taskbar Unresponsive or Start Menu Won't Open
content:
Problem: The Windows taskbar becomes unresponsive, icons stop reacting to clicks, or the Start menu fails to open when clicked.

Symptoms:
- Clicking the Start button, search, or taskbar icons produces no response
- System tray icons and clock may still be visible but non-interactive
- User reports 'my Start menu won't open' or 'taskbar is frozen'
- Other applications may continue to work normally while the taskbar is unresponsive

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Task Manager via Ctrl+Shift+Esc (this often works even when the taskbar is frozen).
2. Locate 'Windows Explorer' in the Processes tab, select it, and click Restart to reload the shell.
3. If Explorer is not listed, click File > Run new task, type explorer.exe, and press Enter.
4. If the issue recurs, check for recent app installs or updates that coincide with the onset of the problem.
5. Run sfc /scannow from an elevated Command Prompt to check for corrupted system files.
6. Create a new local Windows user profile as a test to see if the issue is profile-specific.
7. If the problem persists across profiles and after Explorer restarts, escalate to L2 for deeper investigation.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Taskbar

title: File Explorer Freezes or Crashes When Opening Folders
content:
Problem: File Explorer becomes unresponsive, freezes, or crashes ('File Explorer has stopped working') when the user attempts to open certain folders or browse files.

Symptoms:
- File Explorer window freezes, shows 'Not Responding', or closes unexpectedly
- Issue may occur only in specific folders (e.g., large folders, network shares, OneDrive)
- User reports 'my folders keep freezing' or 'File Explorer keeps crashing'
- Desktop icons and taskbar may also flicker if the crash affects the shell

Resolution Steps:
1. Restart File Explorer via Task Manager (locate 'Windows Explorer', click Restart).
2. Clear File Explorer history and cache via File Explorer Options > General > Clear.
3. Disable Quick Access and recent files display temporarily to see if that resolves the freeze.
4. If the issue is isolated to a specific folder (e.g., a large network share or synced OneDrive folder), test opening a different local folder to confirm.
5. Update or reinstall any shell extensions (e.g., cloud storage or antivirus context-menu add-ons) that may be interfering.
6. Check disk health using chkdsk if freezing correlates with accessing the local hard drive specifically.
7. Escalate to L2 if crashes continue after cache clearing and shell restart, including which folder/path triggers the issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / File Explorer

title: Files or Folders Missing After Windows Update
content:
Problem: Following a Windows feature update or major update installation, a user reports that personal files, folders, or desktop icons appear to be missing.

Symptoms:
- Desktop appears empty or files are missing after an update completed
- User reports 'my files disappeared after the update' or 'I can't find my documents'
- Files may still exist but the desktop/profile path has changed
- Windows.old folder may be present on the C: drive

Resolution Steps:
1. Check for a Windows.old folder at C:\Windows.old, which stores the previous installation's files after a feature update.
2. Search the full C: drive for the specific missing file names using File Explorer search.
3. Check if a second/temporary user profile was created (e.g., username.000) by comparing C:\Users folder contents.
4. If files are in Windows.old, guide the user to copy them back to their current profile, or copy the files for them if permissions allow.
5. Verify OneDrive/known folder redirection settings, as some files may have moved location due to sync configuration changes.
6. Advise the user that Windows.old is typically removed automatically after 10 days, so recovery should not be delayed.
7. Escalate to L2 if files cannot be located anywhere on the system, so a deeper file recovery attempt can be made.

Edge Case: If OneDrive sync was paused or disconnected during the update, files may appear missing locally but still exist safely in the cloud — check the OneDrive web portal before escalating.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Files

title: Application Repeatedly Crashes or Freezes on Windows
content:
Problem: A specific desktop application (not an Office or Microsoft 365 app) repeatedly crashes, freezes, or closes unexpectedly on a Windows laptop.

Symptoms:
- Application closes suddenly, sometimes with a 'has stopped working' dialog
- App may freeze and show 'Not Responding' in the title bar
- User reports 'the program keeps crashing' or 'it closes by itself'
- Crash may happen at launch, during a specific action, or randomly

Resolution Steps:
1. Close and relaunch the application; if it is unresponsive, end the task via Task Manager first.
2. Check for and install any pending application updates from the vendor or the internal Software Portal.
3. Restart the laptop to clear any memory or resource conflicts before retesting.
4. Check Event Viewer (Application log) for the specific error associated with the crash, and note the faulting module name.
5. Run the application as Administrator to rule out permission-related crashes.
6. If a recent Windows Update or app update coincides with the onset of crashes, consider a rollback or reinstall of the affected application.
7. Escalate to L2 with the Event Viewer error details and steps to reproduce if the crash continues after reinstall.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Applications

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) Errors on Windows Laptop
content:
Problem: A Windows laptop unexpectedly displays a Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) with a stop code and restarts, either occasionally or repeatedly.

Symptoms:
- Blue screen appears with a message such as 'Your PC ran into a problem and needs to restart'
- A stop code is shown, e.g., MEMORY_MANAGEMENT, IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, or DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL
- Laptop restarts automatically after the blue screen
- User reports 'blue screen', 'BSOD', or 'crash screen' with error code

Resolution Steps:
1. Record the exact stop code shown on the blue screen or found in Reliability Monitor / Event Viewer (System log, BugCheck event).
2. Note any recent hardware changes, driver installs, or Windows Updates that preceded the first BSOD.
3. Run Windows Memory Diagnostic (mdsched.exe) to rule out faulty RAM.
4. Check Device Manager for any devices with a yellow warning icon indicating a driver conflict.
5. Update or roll back the most recently installed or updated driver, especially graphics and chipset drivers.
6. Run sfc /scannow and DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth to check for system file corruption.
7. Escalate to L2 with the stop code and minidump file location (C:\Windows\Minidump) if BSODs continue after driver and system file checks.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Errors

title: Low Disk Space Warning on Windows Laptop
content:
Problem: Windows displays a low disk space warning, and the user's system drive (typically C:) is nearly full, potentially affecting performance and updates.

Symptoms:
- Notification reads 'Low disk space' or 'You're running low on storage space on Local Disk (C:)'
- File Explorer shows the C: drive bar in red/near capacity
- User reports the laptop 'feels slow' or 'won't let me save files'
- New application installs or updates may fail due to insufficient space

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Settings > System > Storage to see a breakdown of what is consuming space.
2. Run Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr.exe) including 'Clean up system files' to remove temp files, old update files, and Recycle Bin contents.
3. Enable Storage Sense to automatically manage temporary files and Downloads folder cleanup going forward.
4. Identify and offload large local files (videos, ISOs, installers) to OneDrive or an external drive, with user consent.
5. Uninstall unused applications from Settings > Apps that are consuming significant disk space.
6. Check for and remove duplicate or orphaned Windows.old folders if a prior cleanup did not complete.
7. If space remains critically low after cleanup (e.g., under 10 GB free) and cannot be freed further, escalate to consider a storage upgrade.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Storage

title: Slow Windows Performance With High CPU or Memory Usage
content:
Problem: A Windows laptop runs noticeably slowly, with applications taking a long time to open or respond, often correlating with high CPU or memory usage.

Symptoms:
- User reports laptop is 'running slow', 'laggy', or 'takes forever to open anything'
- Task Manager shows CPU or memory usage consistently above 80-90% at idle
- Fan noise may be elevated even when not running demanding applications
- Applications take longer than usual to launch or respond to input

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and sort by CPU and Memory to identify the top resource-consuming processes.
2. Check Startup apps tab in Task Manager and disable unnecessary applications from launching at boot.
3. Confirm antivirus/endpoint protection is not mid-scan, as full system scans commonly cause temporary slowdowns.
4. Check for pending Windows Updates or driver updates that may be running in the background.
5. Restart the laptop, since accumulated memory usage from long uptime is a common cause of gradual slowdown.
6. Verify available disk space and run Disk Cleanup, as a nearly full drive can significantly degrade performance.
7. If a specific process consistently consumes excessive resources with no clear cause, escalate to L2 with the process name and resource usage details.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Performance

title: Windows Display Resolution or Settings Reset After Restart
content:
Problem: Display resolution, scaling, or other Windows display settings revert to defaults or change unexpectedly after every restart or docking/undocking.

Symptoms:
- Screen resolution or scaling changes back to a default value after every reboot
- User reports 'my screen settings keep resetting' or 'resolution changes on its own'
- Issue often correlates with connecting/disconnecting an external monitor or dock
- Taskbar or icon positions may also rearrange unexpectedly

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the current display driver version in Device Manager and check for available updates.
2. Set the desired resolution and scaling manually in Settings > System > Display, then click Keep changes to confirm.
3. If using multiple monitors, verify each display's individual scaling setting rather than relying on a single global setting.
4. Update the graphics driver to the latest version from the manufacturer (Intel/NVIDIA/AMD) rather than relying solely on Windows Update.
5. If the issue occurs specifically when docking/undocking, update the docking station's drivers and firmware as well.
6. Disable and re-enable the display adapter in Device Manager to reset its configuration.
7. Escalate to L2 if settings continue to reset after driver updates, especially if it affects multiple users with the same dock/monitor model.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Settings

title: Device Manager Shows Driver Error Code 10 or 'This Device Cannot Start'
content:
Problem: A system device in Device Manager displays a yellow warning icon with an error such as 'This device cannot start (Code 10)' or similar driver-related error codes.

Symptoms:
- Yellow triangle warning icon next to a device in Device Manager
- Error message reads 'This device cannot start (Code 10)' or comparable code (e.g., Code 28, Code 43)
- Associated hardware function (e.g., chipset feature, network controller) does not work
- User may report a specific feature not working without knowing the underlying driver cause

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Device Manager, right-click the affected device, and select Update driver > Search automatically.
2. If no update is found, uninstall the device (check 'Delete the driver software' if offered) and restart the laptop to let Windows reinstall it.
3. Download the latest driver directly from the manufacturer's support site if Windows Update does not resolve it.
4. Check for and install any pending Windows Updates, as some driver fixes ship through cumulative updates.
5. Verify the device is properly seated/connected if it is an internal expansion component.
6. Use System Restore to roll back to a point before the error appeared if it followed a recent driver or update install.
7. Escalate to L2 with the exact device name and error code if the issue persists after driver reinstall.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Drivers

title: Windows Service Fails to Start (Print Spooler, Windows Update, etc.)
content:
Problem: A critical Windows service such as Print Spooler or Windows Update fails to start, is stuck in a 'Starting' state, or stops unexpectedly, disabling the related functionality.

Symptoms:
- Error message such as 'Print Spooler service is not running' when trying to print
- Windows Update fails to check for updates with a service-related error
- services.msc shows the service status as blank, stopped, or stuck on 'Starting'
- User reports a specific feature (printing, updates) 'just stopped working'

Resolution Steps:
1. Open services.msc, locate the affected service (e.g., Print Spooler, Windows Update), and attempt to start it manually.
2. If it fails to start, check the service's Log On tab to confirm it is using the correct account (typically Local System).
3. Restart dependent services listed under the Dependencies tab, starting with the lowest-level dependency first.
4. For Print Spooler issues, clear the print queue folder at C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS before restarting the service.
5. For Windows Update service issues, reset the service using the built-in Windows Update Troubleshooter.
6. Run sfc /scannow to check for corrupted service-related system files.
7. Escalate to L2 with the exact service name and any error code shown in Event Viewer if the service still will not start.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Windows / Services

title: User Logs In to a Temporary or Corrupted Windows Profile
content:
Problem: A user logs into Windows and is greeted with a message that they have been logged in with a temporary profile, or their desktop appears default/empty with settings and files missing.

Symptoms:
- Notification reads 'You've been logged on with a temporary profile' or similar
- Desktop background, icons, pinned taskbar items, and saved settings are all reset to default
- Previously installed application preferences and saved files in the profile appear missing
- Issue may resolve temporarily after a restart, then recur

Resolution Steps:
1. Have the user log out completely and log back in to see if the correct profile loads.
2. Restart the laptop, as a corrupted profile registry key can sometimes be transient after a crash or forced shutdown.
3. Check the registry under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList for a duplicate profile key ending in .bak, which indicates a known profile corruption pattern.
4. If a .bak duplicate key exists, this requires an L2/admin-level registry fix to rename keys and restore the correct SID mapping — do not edit the registry without following the documented internal procedure.
5. In the interim, advise the user to save any critical files to a network drive or OneDrive to avoid data loss.
6. Check available disk space, as insufficient space during login can also trigger temporary profile creation.
7. Escalate to L2 for profile rebuild if the temporary profile issue recurs after a restart.

Edge Case: Do not delete the affected user profile without confirming files have been backed up, as this is a common way user data is permanently lost.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, Active Directory-joined devices
Category: Windows / User Profile

title: Wi-Fi Won't Connect / 'Can't Connect to This Network'
content:
Problem: A laptop is unable to connect to a Wi-Fi network, either failing silently or showing an explicit error such as 'Can't connect to this network.'

Symptoms:
- Wi-Fi network appears in the list but connection attempts fail or time out
- Error message reads 'Can't connect to this network' or 'Windows was unable to connect'
- User reports 'my Wi-Fi won't connect' or 'wireless network unavailable'
- Other devices may connect to the same network successfully

Resolution Steps:
1. Toggle Wi-Fi off and on via the network flyout or Settings > Network & Internet.
2. Forget the network (Settings > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Forget) and reconnect, re-entering the password.
3. Run the Windows Network Troubleshooter (Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Internet Connections).
4. Restart the wireless adapter via Device Manager (disable, then re-enable).
5. Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver to the latest version from the manufacturer.
6. Move closer to the access point to rule out signal strength as a factor.
7. If the laptop cannot connect while other devices can, escalate to L2 to check for a device-specific network profile or driver issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, all Wi-Fi enabled laptops
Category: Network / Wi-Fi

title: Wi-Fi Connects But No Internet Access
content:
Problem: A laptop shows a successful Wi-Fi connection (connected, full signal bars) but the user cannot browse the internet or reach internal resources.

Symptoms:
- Wi-Fi icon shows connected with strong signal, sometimes with a warning triangle
- Browser shows 'No internet' or pages time out loading
- User reports 'I'm connected to Wi-Fi but nothing loads'
- Message may say 'Connected, no internet' in the network flyout

Resolution Steps:
1. Check if other websites/services work to rule out a single-site outage versus a full connectivity issue.
2. Open Command Prompt and run ipconfig /all to check if a valid IP address, gateway, and DNS server were assigned.
3. Run ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew to request a fresh IP address from DHCP.
4. Run ipconfig /flushdns to clear any stale DNS cache entries.
5. Test connectivity to the gateway with ping <gateway IP>, and to an external IP (e.g., 8.8.8.8) to isolate DNS vs. general connectivity.
6. Restart the wireless router/access point if this is a home or branch office setup within IT's control.
7. Escalate to network team if ipconfig shows no valid IP (APIPA 169.254.x.x address) or if the issue affects multiple users on the same network segment.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / Wi-Fi

title: Wi-Fi Disconnects Frequently / Intermittent Wireless Drops
content:
Problem: A laptop repeatedly loses its Wi-Fi connection throughout the day, reconnecting automatically after a short period, disrupting calls and file transfers.

Symptoms:
- Wireless connection drops every few minutes and then reconnects on its own
- User reports 'my Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting' or 'wireless drops constantly'
- Video calls freeze or disconnect intermittently
- Issue may be worse in certain locations within the office or at home

Resolution Steps:
1. Check the Wi-Fi adapter's power management settings and disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' under Device Manager.
2. Update the wireless adapter driver to the latest version.
3. Disable Wi-Fi power-saving mode in the adapter's advanced properties if present.
4. Forget the network and reconnect to rule out a corrupted saved network profile.
5. Check for interference from nearby devices (microwaves, Bluetooth peripherals) or overlapping Wi-Fi channels if multiple access points are nearby.
6. Move the laptop to test in a different location/access point to determine if the issue is location-specific.
7. Escalate to the network team with timestamps of drops if the issue persists across driver updates and power settings changes, as it may indicate an access point or roaming issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / Wi-Fi

title: Slow Wi-Fi Speeds on Laptop
content:
Problem: A laptop connects to Wi-Fi successfully but experiences significantly slower browsing, download, and streaming speeds compared to other devices on the same network.

Symptoms:
- User reports 'my Wi-Fi is really slow' or 'pages take forever to load'
- Speed test results show much lower throughput than expected for the network
- Other devices on the same Wi-Fi network perform normally
- Streaming or video calls buffer or degrade in quality frequently

Resolution Steps:
1. Run a speed test (e.g., via a trusted internal or public speed test tool) and record the result for comparison.
2. Check the Wi-Fi band in use (2.4GHz vs 5GHz) — 2.4GHz is more prone to congestion and slower speeds; connect to 5GHz if available.
3. Move closer to the access point and retest to rule out signal strength as the cause.
4. Update the wireless adapter driver to the latest version.
5. Check Task Manager for background applications or updates consuming bandwidth (e.g., cloud sync, large downloads).
6. Disable any active VPN temporarily to see if it is contributing to the slowdown (VPN routing can reduce effective speed).
7. Escalate to the network team if speeds remain poor after driver updates and band switching, especially if isolated to specific areas of the building.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / Wi-Fi

title: Limited Connectivity / APIPA Address (169.254.x.x)
content:
Problem: A laptop is unable to obtain a valid IP address from the network's DHCP server and instead receives a self-assigned APIPA address in the 169.254.x.x range, resulting in no network access.

Symptoms:
- Network status shows 'Limited' or 'No internet access, secured'
- ipconfig shows an IPv4 address starting with 169.254
- User reports being connected to Wi-Fi or Ethernet but having no access at all
- Issue may appear after waking from sleep or docking/undocking

Resolution Steps:
1. Run ipconfig /all in Command Prompt to confirm the 169.254.x.x address and identify the affected adapter.
2. Run ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew to request a new address from DHCP.
3. Disconnect and reconnect the network adapter (toggle Wi-Fi, or unplug/replug Ethernet cable).
4. Restart the laptop, as this can clear a stuck network stack state.
5. Disable and re-enable the network adapter via Device Manager.
6. Try a different network port or access point/switch if using a wired connection, to rule out a faulty port.
7. Escalate to the network team if the DHCP server is not responding to multiple devices, as this may indicate a broader DHCP scope or infrastructure issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / IP Configuration

title: DNS Resolution Failures — Websites Won't Load by Name
content:
Problem: A user cannot load websites or internal sites by their domain name, though the network connection is otherwise active; direct IP addresses may still work.

Symptoms:
- Browser shows 'This site can't be reached' or 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN'
- User reports 'websites won't load' or 'the internet is connected but nothing opens'
- Pinging a domain name fails, but pinging an IP address succeeds
- Some sites work while others (especially internal/intranet sites) do not

Resolution Steps:
1. Run ipconfig /flushdns in an elevated Command Prompt to clear the local DNS cache.
2. Test resolution using nslookup <domain> to see if DNS queries are returning results.
3. Confirm the DNS server addresses assigned via ipconfig /all match the expected internal or corporate DNS servers.
4. Try browsing using a direct IP address to confirm the issue is DNS-specific rather than general connectivity.
5. Temporarily switch to a known-good public DNS (e.g., 8.8.8.8) to determine if the issue is with the corporate DNS server itself.
6. Restart the DNS Client service (Dnscache) via services.msc.
7. Escalate to the network team if internal corporate DNS servers are unreachable or returning errors for multiple users.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / DNS

title: Ethernet Connection Not Working / No Network Access via Cable
content:
Problem: A laptop connected via an Ethernet cable (directly or through a dock) shows no network connectivity, despite the cable being properly plugged in.

Symptoms:
- Ethernet icon shows a red X or 'Not connected' despite the cable being plugged in
- Link lights on the Ethernet port/switch do not illuminate
- User reports 'the wired connection isn't working' or 'no internet through the cable'
- Wi-Fi may work fine on the same laptop, isolating the issue to the wired adapter or cable

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the Ethernet cable is firmly seated at both ends and check for visible damage.
2. Test with a different, known-good Ethernet cable to rule out a faulty cable.
3. Try a different Ethernet port on the wall jack, switch, or docking station.
4. Check Device Manager to confirm the Ethernet adapter is enabled and not showing an error.
5. Disable and re-enable the Ethernet adapter, or run ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew.
6. If using a docking station, confirm dock firmware/drivers are up to date, as outdated dock firmware commonly causes Ethernet passthrough issues.
7. Escalate to the network/facilities team if the port shows no link light even with a known-good cable and device, as this may indicate a switch port or wall jack issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, docking stations
Category: Network / Ethernet

title: Network Adapter Missing or Disabled in Device Manager
content:
Problem: A laptop's Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter does not appear at all in Device Manager, or appears with a warning/disabled icon, preventing any network connectivity through that adapter.

Symptoms:
- No wireless or wired network icon appears in the system tray at all
- Device Manager shows the adapter missing, greyed out, or with a down-arrow (disabled) icon
- User reports 'I don't see any Wi-Fi option' or 'my network adapter disappeared'
- May follow a Windows Update, driver rollback, or BIOS change

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Device Manager and check under Network Adapters; if the adapter shows a down arrow, right-click and select Enable device.
2. If the adapter is entirely missing, click Action > Scan for hardware changes in Device Manager.
3. Check Windows Update for any pending driver updates related to networking.
4. Reinstall the adapter driver by uninstalling the device (without deleting driver software first) and restarting to allow Windows to redetect it.
5. If still missing, download and manually install the correct driver from the manufacturer's website using another working device or USB drive.
6. Check BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm the wireless or LAN adapter has not been disabled at the hardware level.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if the adapter does not reappear after driver reinstall and BIOS check, as it may indicate hardware failure.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / Adapter

title: IP Address Conflict / Duplicate IP Detected
content:
Problem: Windows displays a warning that another device on the network is using the same IP address, resulting in intermittent or complete loss of connectivity.

Symptoms:
- Notification reads 'There is an IP address conflict with another system on the network'
- Network connectivity is intermittent or drops shortly after connecting
- User reports random disconnects coinciding with the conflict notification
- Issue may occur more often with statically assigned IP addresses

Resolution Steps:
1. Run ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew to request a new address from DHCP.
2. Confirm the adapter is set to 'Obtain an IP address automatically' rather than a static IP, unless static addressing is required and properly reserved.
3. Restart the laptop to fully release and reacquire network settings.
4. If a static IP is required for this device, verify with the network team that the address is properly reserved/excluded from the DHCP pool.
5. Disconnect and reconnect to the network to force a fresh DHCP lease.
6. Check if the issue coincides with another specific known device (e.g., a personal hotspot or misconfigured printer) that may be statically set to the same range.
7. Escalate to the network team with the conflicting IP address noted in the Windows notification for further investigation.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / IP Configuration

title: Cannot Connect to Corporate Wi-Fi After Password/Certificate Change (802.1X)
content:
Problem: A user who previously connected successfully to the corporate 802.1X-secured Wi-Fi network is now unable to authenticate, typically following a password change or certificate expiration.

Symptoms:
- Wi-Fi prompts repeatedly for credentials or fails authentication immediately
- Error may reference 'authentication failed' or the network requires re-entry of credentials
- User reports the Wi-Fi 'stopped working after I changed my password'
- Personal or guest Wi-Fi networks continue to work normally on the same device

Resolution Steps:
1. Forget the corporate Wi-Fi network profile via Settings > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Forget.
2. Reconnect to the network and enter the updated corporate credentials when prompted.
3. If a client certificate is used instead of a password, check the certificate's validity and expiration date in the Certificate Manager (certmgr.msc).
4. If the certificate has expired, this typically requires the device to be reconnected to the domain/MDM to reissue it — escalate to identity/endpoint management team.
5. Confirm the account is not locked out in Active Directory/Entra ID, which can also block 802.1X authentication.
6. Restart the laptop after credential updates to ensure the new password is used for network authentication as well as Windows login.
7. Escalate to the network team if authentication continues to fail with confirmed correct, unlocked credentials.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, 802.1X-secured Wi-Fi networks
Category: Network / Wi-Fi

title: VPN Client Fails to Connect / 'Unable to Establish VPN Connection'
content:
Problem: A user's VPN client (e.g., Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect) fails to establish a connection to the corporate network, showing a generic connection error.

Symptoms:
- Error message reads 'Unable to establish VPN connection' or 'Connection attempt has failed'
- VPN client hangs at 'Connecting...' before timing out
- User reports 'VPN won't connect' or 'can't get on the VPN'
- Issue may occur on any network (home Wi-Fi, hotel, mobile hotspot)

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the laptop has a working internet connection independent of the VPN by browsing to a public website first.
2. Restart the VPN client application completely (quit from system tray, not just close the window) and relaunch.
3. Restart the VPN client's background service via services.msc (e.g., Cisco AnyConnect VPN Agent).
4. Confirm the correct VPN gateway/server address is selected in the client.
5. Temporarily disable third-party firewall or security software that may be blocking the VPN tunnel (never disable corporate endpoint protection without following policy).
6. Try connecting from a different network (e.g., mobile hotspot) to rule out a local network/firewall block on the current network (e.g., hotel Wi-Fi blocking VPN ports).
7. Escalate to the network team with the exact error text and network location if the issue persists across networks and after client restart.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect, Zscaler
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: VPN Authentication Failure / Login Rejected
content:
Problem: A user can reach the VPN login prompt but their credentials are rejected, preventing the VPN tunnel from establishing even though the same credentials work for other systems.

Symptoms:
- VPN client shows 'Authentication failed' or 'Login denied' after entering credentials
- Username/password combination works for email and other company systems
- User reports 'my VPN says my password is wrong even though it's right'
- May occur immediately after a password change or MFA enrollment change

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the account is not locked out in Active Directory/Entra ID due to repeated failed VPN attempts.
2. Verify the user is entering the correct username format required by the VPN (e.g., domain\username vs. email address).
3. If MFA is required for VPN login, confirm the user is approving the push notification or entering the current one-time code promptly.
4. Have the user retype the password manually rather than using a saved/cached credential, in case of a stale saved password.
5. Restart the VPN client and retry after confirming credentials via a successful login to another company system (e.g., email).
6. Check with identity/security team whether the VPN's authentication backend (RADIUS/LDAP/SAML) is experiencing any known issues.
7. Escalate to network/security team with timestamps of failed attempts if authentication continues to fail with confirmed-correct credentials.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: VPN Connects But Cannot Access Internal Resources
content:
Problem: A user successfully connects to the VPN (shown as connected in the client) but is unable to reach internal resources such as file shares, intranet sites, or internal applications.

Symptoms:
- VPN client shows 'Connected' with a valid session duration
- User can browse the public internet normally while connected
- Internal file shares, intranet sites, or internal apps time out or show 'cannot be reached'
- User reports 'VPN is connected but I can't get to anything internal'

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the VPN client shows an assigned internal IP address (via ipconfig /all) consistent with the corporate VPN subnet.
2. Test access to an internal resource by IP address rather than hostname to determine if this is a DNS issue over VPN.
3. Run ipconfig /flushdns after confirming VPN connection to clear any stale DNS entries pointing to non-VPN routes.
4. Confirm split-tunneling configuration is correct — if split tunneling is misconfigured, internal traffic may be routed outside the VPN tunnel.
5. Disconnect and reconnect the VPN session to refresh routing tables.
6. Test from a different network location to rule out local network routing conflicts (e.g., home router using the same subnet as the corporate network).
7. Escalate to the network team with the internal resource name/IP that is unreachable, as this may indicate a routing or firewall rule issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: VPN Disconnects After Several Minutes of Inactivity
content:
Problem: A user's VPN connection drops automatically after a period of inactivity or idle time, requiring them to reconnect repeatedly throughout the day.

Symptoms:
- VPN session disconnects consistently after roughly 10-30 minutes without active use
- User reports 'my VPN keeps dropping' or 'I have to reconnect every few minutes'
- Disconnection often coincides with the laptop going to sleep or the screen locking
- Active file transfers or long-running sessions are interrupted

Resolution Steps:
1. Check the laptop's power/sleep settings and confirm the device is not set to sleep or hibernate quickly while on battery or plugged in.
2. Check the VPN client's own idle timeout setting, if configurable, and confirm it aligns with company policy.
3. Disable Wi-Fi adapter power-saving mode (Device Manager > Network Adapter > Power Management) which can interrupt VPN sessions.
4. Confirm whether the disconnect correlates with screen lock; some VPN clients disconnect on lock by design per security policy — clarify expected behavior with the user.
5. Update the VPN client to the latest version, as idle-disconnect bugs are sometimes addressed in client updates.
6. Test on a wired Ethernet connection to rule out Wi-Fi power management as the root cause.
7. Escalate to the network team if disconnects continue after power settings and client updates, especially if session timeout should be longer per policy.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: VPN Client Fails to Launch or Open
content:
Problem: The VPN client application does not open at all when launched — no window appears, or it crashes immediately on startup, preventing the user from even attempting to connect.

Symptoms:
- Double-clicking the VPN client icon produces no visible window
- VPN client process may appear briefly in Task Manager then disappear
- User reports 'the VPN app won't open' or 'nothing happens when I click it'
- May follow a recent Windows Update or VPN client update

Resolution Steps:
1. Check Task Manager to confirm whether the VPN client process is running in the background despite no visible window.
2. Restart the VPN client's background service via services.msc, then relaunch the application.
3. Restart the laptop fully and attempt to launch the VPN client again.
4. Check Event Viewer (Application log) for a crash event tied to the VPN client executable.
5. Repair or reinstall the VPN client via Control Panel > Programs, or the internal Software Portal.
6. Confirm the VPN client is not blocked by a recent antivirus/endpoint protection policy update.
7. Escalate to L2 with the Event Viewer crash details if reinstalling the client does not resolve the launch failure.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: VPN Connection Times Out During Handshake
content:
Problem: A VPN connection attempt hangs at a 'Negotiating' or 'Establishing' stage and eventually fails with a timeout error before completing the connection handshake.

Symptoms:
- VPN client progress shows 'Negotiating connection' or 'Establishing VPN' and then times out
- Error message may reference a timeout, such as 'The VPN connection failed due to unsuccessful domain name resolution' or a generic timeout
- User reports the VPN 'just hangs and then fails' after a long wait
- May be more common on certain networks (hotel, public Wi-Fi, mobile hotspot) than on trusted networks

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the underlying network connection is stable and has reasonable latency before attempting VPN again.
2. Try connecting to a different VPN gateway/server if multiple options are available in the client.
3. Check whether the current network blocks the VPN protocol/ports in use (common on hotel or public Wi-Fi networks that restrict UDP/non-standard ports).
4. Switch the VPN client to a different transport protocol if supported (e.g., TCP fallback instead of UDP) to work around port restrictions.
5. Restart the VPN client service and relaunch the application before retrying.
6. Test the connection attempt from a mobile hotspot to isolate whether the current network is blocking the handshake.
7. Escalate to the network team with the network location and exact timeout message if the handshake consistently fails on trusted/office networks.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: Slow Performance or High Latency While Connected to VPN
content:
Problem: Applications, file transfers, and browsing become noticeably slower whenever the user is connected to the VPN, even though the underlying internet connection tests normally without VPN.

Symptoms:
- User reports 'everything is slow when I'm on VPN' or 'VPN makes my internet crawl'
- Speed test results drop significantly while connected to VPN compared to disconnected
- Video calls or streaming buffer or lag specifically while VPN is active
- Local, non-corporate websites may also feel slow if full tunneling is in effect

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm baseline internet speed without VPN connected to establish a comparison point.
2. Check whether split tunneling is enabled/expected for this VPN profile — full tunneling routes all traffic (including general browsing) through the VPN, which can reduce speed for non-corporate sites.
3. Try connecting to a different VPN gateway/region if multiple options are available, as the assigned gateway may be under heavy load.
4. Close bandwidth-heavy background applications (cloud sync, large downloads) while on VPN.
5. Test the connection at a different time of day to rule out peak-hour congestion on the VPN gateway.
6. Update the VPN client to the latest version, as performance improvements are commonly included in updates.
7. Escalate to the network team with speed test results (with and without VPN) if the discrepancy is significant and persistent.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: Proxy Configuration Errors Blocking Internet Access
content:
Problem: A user cannot browse the internet or access certain sites because the laptop's proxy settings are misconfigured, missing, or pointing to an unreachable proxy server.

Symptoms:
- Browser displays 'Unable to connect to the proxy server' or similar error
- Internet works in some applications but not in the browser, or vice versa
- User reports 'the internet doesn't work in Chrome/Edge but works elsewhere'
- Proxy settings in Windows may show an outdated or incorrect address

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy and review the current configuration (manual vs. automatic).
2. If 'Automatically detect settings' is enabled but failing, confirm the correct setup script (PAC file) URL with IT documentation and verify it loads.
3. If a manual proxy address is set incorrectly, correct it to match the current documented corporate proxy address and port.
4. Clear the browser's cache and restart the browser after updating proxy settings.
5. Test connectivity to the proxy server itself (e.g., via ping or telnet to the proxy port) to confirm it is reachable from the current network.
6. Try toggling proxy settings off temporarily (if policy allows) to confirm the proxy is indeed the cause versus a general connectivity issue.
7. Escalate to the network team if the documented proxy server/PAC file is unreachable for multiple users.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, Chrome, Edge, Firefox
Category: Network / Proxy

title: Browser Cannot Reach Internal Sites / SSL Certificate Errors
content:
Problem: A user's browser shows SSL/TLS certificate warnings or refuses to load internal company websites, even though external websites load normally.

Symptoms:
- Browser shows 'Your connection is not private' or 'NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID' for internal sites
- External sites (e.g., google.com) load without any certificate warnings
- User reports 'I get a security warning when I try to open our internal site'
- Issue may be new for the user or follow a recent laptop reimage or new device setup

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the exact internal site URL and error message, and check whether the issue is happening for other users on the same site.
2. Verify the internal Root/Intermediate Certificate Authority (CA) certificate is installed in the Windows Trusted Root store (certmgr.msc).
3. If missing, install the correct internal root CA certificate from the internal Software Portal or via the standard device provisioning process.
4. Confirm the system date and time are correct, as an incorrect clock commonly causes certificate validation failures.
5. Clear the browser cache and restart the browser after confirming certificate installation.
6. Test the same internal site in a different browser to determine if the issue is browser-specific or system-wide.
7. Escalate to the security/PKI team if the internal CA certificate is missing across multiple new or reimaged devices.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, Chrome, Edge, Firefox
Category: Network / Browser Connectivity

title: Wrong VPN Profile or Gateway Selected Causing Connection Issues
content:
Problem: A user has multiple VPN profiles or gateways configured in their client and is inadvertently connecting to the wrong one, resulting in access issues or unexpected routing behavior.

Symptoms:
- User has access to some resources but not others depending on which profile is selected
- VPN client dropdown shows multiple gateway/profile options (e.g., regional gateways, test vs. production)
- User reports inconsistent access 'sometimes I can get to things, sometimes I can't'
- Issue may follow onboarding to a new project, region change, or team transfer

Resolution Steps:
1. Ask the user which VPN profile/gateway they currently have selected in the client dropdown.
2. Confirm with the user's manager or access documentation which gateway is correct for their role/location/project.
3. Have the user switch to the correct profile and reconnect, then retest access to the affected resources.
4. Remove outdated or unnecessary VPN profiles from the client to reduce future confusion, if permitted by policy.
5. Check whether the correct profile requires a separate provisioning/access request if the user does not see it as an option at all.
6. Document which gateway maps to which resource set for the user's reference going forward.
7. Escalate to the network/access team if the correct profile is not available to the user and needs to be provisioned.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS, enterprise VPN clients
Category: Network / VPN

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: Outlook Not Sending or Receiving Emails
content:
Problem: Outlook appears open and connected but emails are not sending (stuck in Outbox) or not receiving new messages, despite other Microsoft 365 apps working normally.

Symptoms:
- Emails remain stuck in the Outbox with a 'Sending' status that never completes
- No new emails arrive despite confirmation they were sent by others
- User reports 'Outlook isn't sending or receiving anything'
- Status bar may show 'Trying to connect' or 'Disconnected'

Resolution Steps:
1. Check the connection status in the bottom-right of Outlook; if it shows 'Disconnected' or 'Working Offline', click to toggle back online.
2. Confirm general internet connectivity is working by browsing to a website.
3. Restart Outlook completely (ensure it is fully closed via Task Manager, not just minimized).
4. Check Outlook's Send/Receive settings (Send/Receive tab) and manually trigger Send/Receive All Folders.
5. Verify the mailbox is not near or over its storage quota, which can block sending.
6. Check for oversized attachments on stuck emails in the Outbox, as these commonly cause sends to hang.
7. If issue persists, have the user test Outlook Web Access (OWA) to determine if the issue is client-specific or mailbox/server-side, and escalate accordingly.

Affected Systems: Outlook (Desktop), Outlook Web Access, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Outlook Search Not Returning Results
content:
Problem: Searching for emails within Outlook returns no results, incomplete results, or only very old/new emails, even though the target message is known to exist in the mailbox.

Symptoms:
- Search bar returns 'No results found' for emails known to exist
- Search only returns results from a limited date range
- User reports 'Outlook search isn't working' or 'I can't find old emails'
- Message may appear in Outlook Web Access search but not in the desktop client, or vice versa

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the search scope is set to 'All Mailboxes' or 'All Outlook Items' rather than a single folder.
2. Rebuild the Windows Search index for Outlook via Control Panel > Indexing Options > Modify > ensure Outlook is checked.
3. Check indexing status via Outlook: File > Options > Search > Indexing Options, and confirm indexing is complete (not paused).
4. If indexing is incomplete, allow time for it to finish, or click 'Rebuild' if it appears stuck.
5. Test the same search in Outlook Web Access (OWA) to determine if the issue is local indexing versus a server-side/mailbox issue.
6. Restart Outlook and, if needed, restart the laptop to allow the search index service to restart cleanly.
7. Escalate to L2 if the index remains stuck at a low percentage or search fails consistently after a rebuild attempt.

Affected Systems: Outlook (Desktop), Outlook Web Access, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Outlook Repeatedly Prompts for Password / Cannot Stay Signed In
content:
Problem: Outlook continually prompts the user to re-enter their password, even after successful sign-in, and the credential prompt reappears within minutes.

Symptoms:
- A 'Need Password' or sign-in dialog appears repeatedly in Outlook, often every few minutes
- Entering correct credentials does not stop the prompts from recurring
- User reports 'Outlook keeps asking for my password' or 'it won't stay logged in'
- Other Microsoft 365 apps (Teams, OneDrive) may or may not show the same behavior

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the account is not locked out or requiring a password reset via the Microsoft 365 admin portal or self-service portal.
2. Clear saved/cached credentials for Outlook via Control Panel > Credential Manager, removing entries related to Office/Outlook.
3. Check whether Modern Authentication is properly enabled for the account, as legacy auth prompts can loop under certain configurations.
4. Close Outlook fully, then sign out and back into the Windows/Office account via Settings > Accounts > Access work or school account.
5. Update Outlook to the latest version via File > Office Account > Update Options > Update Now.
6. Check Credential Manager and Windows accounts for a duplicate or conflicting cached identity, especially if the user recently changed their password.
7. Escalate to identity/security team if the loop persists after clearing cached credentials and confirming the account is not locked, as it may indicate a conditional access or token issue.

Affected Systems: Outlook (Desktop), Microsoft 365, Modern Authentication
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Shared Mailbox Not Appearing or Not Syncing in Outlook
content:
Problem: A user with confirmed access to a shared mailbox does not see it listed in Outlook, or it appears but does not sync new emails.

Symptoms:
- Shared mailbox does not appear in the folder list despite the user having permissions
- Shared mailbox appears but new emails do not show up without a manual refresh
- User reports 'I can't see the shared inbox' or 'the shared mailbox isn't updating'
- Shared mailbox may be visible correctly in Outlook Web Access but not in the desktop client

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm with the mailbox owner/admin that the user has been granted Full Access permission (not just Send As) to the shared mailbox.
2. Allow up to several hours for newly granted permissions to replicate across Microsoft 365 before troubleshooting further.
3. Have the user manually add the shared mailbox via File > Account Settings > Account Settings > double-click their account > Advanced > Add the shared mailbox.
4. If already added but not syncing, remove and re-add the shared mailbox to force a fresh sync.
5. Check if the shared mailbox is set to 'Download shared folders' in Outlook's Advanced account settings.
6. Test access via Outlook Web Access (OWA) to confirm the permissions are correctly applied at the server/mailbox level.
7. Escalate to the Exchange/M365 admin team if permissions are confirmed correct in the admin center but the mailbox still fails to sync in the desktop client.

Affected Systems: Outlook (Desktop), Outlook Web Access, Exchange Online
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Outlook Calendar Invites Not Syncing / Missing Meetings
content:
Problem: A user reports that meeting invites they accepted do not appear on their calendar, or meetings disappear unexpectedly, causing them to miss appointments.

Symptoms:
- Accepted meeting invites do not show on the calendar in Outlook
- Meetings that previously appeared have disappeared without user action
- User reports 'I accepted the invite but it's not on my calendar' or 'meetings keep vanishing'
- Calendar may show correctly in Outlook Web Access but not in the desktop client, or vice versa

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the meeting invite was actually accepted (not just previewed) and check the Deleted Items folder for a possible accidental deletion.
2. Check if a calendar sharing/delegate rule or mailbox rule is inadvertently moving or deleting meeting invites.
3. Compare the calendar view in Outlook Web Access against the desktop client to isolate whether this is a sync issue or a server-side issue.
4. Force a manual Send/Receive in the desktop client to refresh calendar data.
5. Check for and disable any third-party calendar sync add-ins that might be interfering.
6. Recreate the Outlook profile (Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles) if the calendar consistently fails to sync in the desktop client only.
7. Escalate to the Exchange/M365 admin team if the meeting is confirmed present on the server (via OWA) but never appears in the desktop client after profile recreation.

Affected Systems: Outlook (Desktop), Outlook Web Access, Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 Calendar
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Teams Meeting Audio Not Working (Can't Hear or Be Heard)
content:
Problem: During a Microsoft Teams meeting, a user cannot hear other participants, or other participants cannot hear the user, despite audio appearing to be connected.

Symptoms:
- User reports 'I can't hear anyone' or 'no one can hear me' during a Teams call
- Teams shows the microphone/speaker icons as active with no visible error
- Audio may work in one direction only (can hear but not be heard, or vice versa)
- Issue may be specific to Teams while other applications' audio works fine

Resolution Steps:
1. In the Teams meeting, click the '...' menu and select Device Settings to confirm the correct microphone and speaker are selected.
2. Test the microphone and speaker via Teams' built-in 'Make a test call' feature found in Settings > Devices.
3. Check the Windows volume mixer to confirm Teams is not muted at the system level and volume is not set to zero.
4. Confirm the physical mute button on a headset (if present) is not engaged.
5. Leave and rejoin the meeting, as this often resolves a stuck audio session.
6. Restart the Teams application completely (quit from system tray, not just close the window).
7. If the issue persists across meetings and after a Teams restart, escalate to L2 with the headset/audio device model for driver-level investigation.

Affected Systems: Microsoft Teams (Desktop), Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Software / Collaboration

title: Teams Camera/Video Not Working During Meetings
content:
Problem: A user's webcam does not activate or shows a black screen when turning on video during a Microsoft Teams meeting, even though the camera works in other applications.

Symptoms:
- Teams video preview shows a black screen or 'Your video isn't working' message
- Camera light does not turn on when toggling video in Teams
- User reports 'my camera won't turn on in Teams' or 'video shows black'
- Webcam may function correctly in the Windows Camera app or other video applications

Resolution Steps:
1. Check Windows privacy settings (Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera) to confirm Teams is allowed access to the camera.
2. In Teams, go to Settings > Devices and confirm the correct camera is selected from the dropdown.
3. Close any other application that may be using the camera simultaneously (only one app can typically access it at a time).
4. Restart the Teams application completely and rejoin the meeting.
5. Test the camera in the Windows Camera app to confirm it works outside of Teams.
6. Update the webcam driver via Device Manager if the camera fails in all applications, not just Teams.
7. Escalate to L2 with the webcam make/model if the camera works elsewhere but never in Teams after cache clearing and permission checks.

Affected Systems: Microsoft Teams (Desktop), Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Software / Collaboration

title: Teams Messages Not Syncing / Notifications Delayed
content:
Problem: Microsoft Teams chat messages or channel notifications arrive significantly delayed, or messages sent by the user do not appear on their other signed-in devices.

Symptoms:
- Notifications for new Teams messages arrive minutes late or not at all
- Messages sent from one device do not immediately appear on another signed-in device
- User reports 'my Teams notifications are delayed' or 'messages aren't syncing between my devices'
- Teams may show as 'Connecting' or take a long time to load chats on launch

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm Teams is fully updated to the latest version via the '...' menu > Check for updates.
2. Sign out of Teams completely and sign back in to refresh the session.
3. Clear the Teams cache by closing Teams and deleting the contents of the Teams cache folder (%appdata%\Microsoft\Teams), then relaunch.
4. Check Windows notification settings (Settings > System > Notifications) to confirm Teams notifications are enabled and not set to 'Priority only'.
5. Confirm Focus Assist / Do Not Disturb is not suppressing notifications unexpectedly.
6. Check internet connectivity stability, as intermittent drops can delay Teams' real-time sync.
7. Escalate to L2 if delays persist after a cache clear and re-authentication, especially if affecting multiple users at once (possible service-side issue).

Affected Systems: Microsoft Teams (Desktop), Microsoft Teams (Web), Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Collaboration

title: Teams Presence/Status Stuck or Not Updating
content:
Problem: A user's Microsoft Teams presence status (Available, Away, Busy, etc.) does not update correctly, remaining stuck on one status regardless of actual activity or calendar state.

Symptoms:
- Status remains 'Away' even while actively using the laptop
- Status does not automatically change to 'In a meeting' or 'Busy' during scheduled calendar events
- User reports 'my Teams status is stuck' or 'it always shows me as away'
- Manually setting status works temporarily but reverts on its own

Resolution Steps:
1. Manually set the correct status in Teams to confirm the change takes effect at all.
2. Check if 'Duration' was set on a manual status (e.g., 'Away until I sign in again'), which can override automatic detection.
3. Sign out of Teams and sign back in to refresh the presence sync with Outlook calendar.
4. Confirm system idle/sleep settings are not causing Windows to report inactivity prematurely.
5. Clear the Teams cache (%appdata%\Microsoft\Teams) and relaunch the application.
6. Check if the user is signed into Teams on multiple devices with conflicting manually-set statuses.
7. Escalate to L2 if presence remains incorrect after cache clearing and re-authentication, noting whether it affects calendar-based status changes specifically.

Affected Systems: Microsoft Teams (Desktop), Microsoft Teams (Web), Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Collaboration

title: Teams Screen Sharing Fails or Freezes
content:
Problem: A user attempting to share their screen in a Teams meeting either cannot start the share, or the shared screen freezes/lags significantly for other participants.

Symptoms:
- Clicking 'Share' in Teams produces an error or the share never starts
- Shared screen freezes on a single frame while the presenter continues working
- Other participants report choppy, frozen, or heavily delayed screen share
- User reports 'my screen share isn't working' or 'people say my share is frozen'

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the correct screen or window is selected in the share picker, not an incorrect monitor.
2. Check Windows privacy settings (Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen recording, if applicable) to ensure Teams has permission.
3. Close unnecessary applications and browser tabs to free up system resources, as screen sharing is CPU-intensive.
4. Restart the Teams application completely and rejoin the meeting before attempting to share again.
5. Update graphics drivers, as outdated GPU drivers are a common cause of screen share freezing.
6. Test with a wired Ethernet connection instead of Wi-Fi if bandwidth/latency may be contributing to freezing.
7. Escalate to L2 with laptop specs and network conditions if screen sharing consistently fails or freezes after driver updates.

Affected Systems: Microsoft Teams (Desktop), Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Software / Collaboration

title: OneDrive Files Not Syncing / Stuck on 'Processing Changes'
content:
Problem: OneDrive stops syncing files, with the sync icon showing a perpetual spinning/processing state, or newly saved files never upload to the cloud.

Symptoms:
- OneDrive icon in the system tray shows a spinning sync icon that never completes
- Status reads 'Processing changes' for an extended period (hours)
- New or edited files do not show the green checkmark indicating successful sync
- User reports 'OneDrive isn't syncing' or 'files are stuck uploading'

Resolution Steps:
1. Click the OneDrive icon in the system tray to check for specific error messages or files listed as problematic.
2. Pause and resume OneDrive sync (right-click the tray icon > Pause syncing, wait, then Resume syncing).
3. Check for files with unsupported characters, excessively long path names, or that are open in another application, as these commonly block sync.
4. Sign out of OneDrive and sign back in (Settings gear > Account > sign out, then relaunch and sign in).
5. Confirm sufficient local disk space is available, as low disk space can halt syncing.
6. Restart the OneDrive process via Task Manager, or run the OneDrive reset command (onedrive.exe /reset) from the Run dialog.
7. Escalate to L2 if syncing remains stuck after reset, noting the specific file(s) or folder(s) reported as problematic.

Affected Systems: OneDrive (Desktop), Windows 10, Windows 11, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: OneDrive Sync Conflicts / Duplicate Files Created
content:
Problem: OneDrive creates duplicate copies of files, often appended with '-Copy', the computer name, or a username, when the same file is edited from multiple devices or offline.

Symptoms:
- Multiple versions of the same file appear with suffixes like 'filename-ComputerName.docx' or 'filename (1).xlsx'
- User reports 'OneDrive made two copies of my file' or 'there's a duplicate with my computer's name on it'
- Conflicting edits may have been made while offline on two different devices
- Confusion over which version contains the most recent/correct changes

Resolution Steps:
1. Open both/all conflicting file versions and compare content to determine which contains the correct or most recent changes.
2. Manually merge any needed content from the duplicate into the primary file, then delete the unnecessary duplicate(s).
3. Explain to the user that this occurs when the same file is edited on two devices while one was offline, resulting in a sync conflict.
4. Check OneDrive's version history (right-click file > Version History, or via the OneDrive web interface) to recover specific prior versions if needed.
5. Advise the user to ensure only one device is used to edit a given file at a time when working offline, where possible.
6. For frequently conflicting shared files, recommend co-authoring in the Office web/desktop app instead of local editing to avoid conflicts.
7. Escalate to L2 if conflicts are happening frequently without an offline-editing explanation, as it may indicate a sync engine issue.

Affected Systems: OneDrive (Desktop), Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: SharePoint Site Access Denied / Permission Errors
content:
Problem: A user attempting to access a SharePoint site or document library receives an 'Access Denied' or 'Sorry, you need permission to access this site' error.

Symptoms:
- Browser displays 'Access Denied' or 'You need permission to access this site' when navigating to a SharePoint URL
- User previously had access, or is a new hire/recently transferred employee expecting access
- Requesting access via SharePoint's built-in request button produces no response or goes to the wrong approver
- Issue may be specific to one site while other SharePoint sites work normally

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm with the user the exact SharePoint site URL and what access level they expect (view, edit, etc.).
2. Check with the site owner or via the SharePoint admin center whether the user is currently a member of the site or its associated security group.
