3. If access should exist, verify group membership sync has completed, as Entra ID group changes can take time to propagate to SharePoint permissions.
4. Have the user try accessing the site in an incognito/private browser window to rule out a cached credential or session issue.
5. Clear browser cache and cookies for the SharePoint domain, then retry.
6. Confirm the user is signed into the browser with the correct company account, especially if multiple Microsoft accounts are signed in simultaneously.
7. If access should be granted but is missing, submit or escalate an access request to the site owner or SharePoint admin per the standard access request process.

Affected Systems: SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: SharePoint Files Won't Open or Load Slowly
content:
Problem: Documents stored on a SharePoint site take an excessively long time to open, time out, or fail to load entirely, whether accessed via browser or a desktop Office application.

Symptoms:
- Clicking a SharePoint document link results in a long loading spinner or eventual timeout
- User reports 'SharePoint files take forever to open' or 'documents won't load'
- Issue may be specific to large files, certain libraries, or occur across the entire site
- Files may open fine when downloaded locally but not when opened directly from SharePoint

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm general internet/network connectivity is stable and not the underlying cause.
2. Try opening the file in a different browser or in Incognito/InPrivate mode to rule out browser extensions or cache issues.
3. Clear the browser cache and cookies for the SharePoint/Office domains.
4. If opening via desktop Office apps, check File > Info for sync status and try File > Open > Browse to reselect the SharePoint location.
5. Test opening a different, smaller file on the same SharePoint site to determine if the issue is file-size or site-wide.
6. Check the file size and format — very large files (e.g., large Excel workbooks with heavy formulas) can be slow to open even under normal conditions.
7. Escalate to L2 or the SharePoint admin team if the issue affects an entire site or multiple users, or if large files consistently time out.

Affected Systems: SharePoint Online, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Word, Excel, or PowerPoint Crashes on Launch
content:
Problem: A Microsoft Office application (Word, Excel, or PowerPoint) crashes immediately upon opening, either closing silently or showing a 'has stopped working' error before the user can do anything.

Symptoms:
- Application briefly flashes open then closes immediately
- Error dialog reads 'Microsoft Word has stopped working' (or Excel/PowerPoint equivalent)
- User reports 'Excel won't open at all' or 'Word crashes as soon as I click it'
- Other Office apps may continue to work normally while one specific app crashes

Resolution Steps:
1. Attempt to open the application in Safe Mode by holding Ctrl while launching, to determine if an add-in is causing the crash.
2. If Safe Mode launch succeeds, go to File > Options > Add-ins > COM Add-ins > Go, and disable recently added or third-party add-ins.
3. Repair the Office installation via Control Panel > Programs > Microsoft 365/Office > Change > Quick Repair; use Online Repair if Quick Repair does not resolve it.
4. Check for and install pending Office updates via File > Account > Update Options > Update Now.
5. Create a new Windows user profile as a test to determine if the crash is specific to the current profile.
6. Check Event Viewer (Application log) for the specific faulting module associated with the crash.
7. Escalate to L2 with the Event Viewer details if the crash persists after a Quick Repair, Online Repair, and add-in disabling.

Affected Systems: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Microsoft 365, Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Excel File Corrupted or Fails to Save Changes
content:
Problem: An Excel workbook either shows signs of corruption when opened (garbled data, repair prompts) or fails to save changes, sometimes returning an error or silently not persisting edits.

Symptoms:
- Excel shows a message such as 'Excel found unreadable content' or prompts to repair the file on open
- Saving produces an error like 'Document not saved' or the save appears to succeed but changes are lost on reopen
- User reports 'my Excel file is corrupted' or 'my changes keep disappearing'
- File may be stored on OneDrive/SharePoint or a local/network drive

Resolution Steps:
1. If prompted, allow Excel's built-in repair feature to attempt automatic recovery when opening the file.
2. Check OneDrive/SharePoint version history (right-click file > Version History) to restore a known-good previous version.
3. If saving locally fails, try Save As to a new file name/location to determine if the original file path or file itself is the issue.
4. Confirm the file is not open by another user or in a conflicting co-authoring session that might be blocking the save.
5. Check available disk space and network connectivity if the file is stored on a network share or cloud location.
6. Disable any recently added Excel add-ins that may be interfering with the save process (File > Options > Add-ins).
7. Escalate to L2 with the original file location and exact error message if repair and version history do not recover a usable file.

Affected Systems: Excel, Microsoft 365, OneDrive, SharePoint
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Microsoft 365 Sign-In Loop / 'We Can't Sign You In'
content:
Problem: A user attempting to sign into any Microsoft 365 application is caught in a repeating sign-in prompt, or receives an error stating 'We can't sign you in' or similar, without ever reaching their account.

Symptoms:
- Sign-in window reopens repeatedly without ever completing authentication
- Error message reads 'We can't sign you in' or 'Something went wrong'
- Issue may affect all Microsoft 365 apps (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive) simultaneously
- User reports 'I can't log into Office at all' or 'it just keeps asking me to sign in'

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the account is not locked out and the password is current via a successful sign-in to a known-working service (e.g., the company portal or webmail).
2. Clear cached credentials via Control Panel > Credential Manager, removing all Office/Microsoft-related entries.
3. Sign out of all Microsoft accounts on the device via Settings > Accounts > Email & accounts / Access work or school account, then sign back in.
4. Check the system date and time for accuracy, as incorrect time can cause authentication token validation failures.
5. Clear the Office/Microsoft 365 credential cache located under %localappdata%\Microsoft\Office\16.0\.
6. Test sign-in from a different network (e.g., mobile hotspot) to rule out a network-level block on authentication endpoints.
7. Escalate to identity/security team if sign-in continues to fail across apps and networks, as it may indicate a conditional access policy or account-level issue.

Affected Systems: Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Office Activation Error / 'Unlicensed Product' Notice
content:
Problem: Microsoft Office applications display an 'Unlicensed Product' banner or activation error, and premium features become greyed out or unavailable despite the user having an assigned license.

Symptoms:
- Red 'Unlicensed Product' banner appears at the top of Word, Excel, or PowerPoint
- Editing features are greyed out or the app opens in a limited/view-only functionality mode
- User reports 'Office says it's not activated' or 'I can't edit, it says unlicensed'
- Issue may follow a laptop reimage, new device setup, or a change in license assignment

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the user has an active Microsoft 365 license assigned in the admin center (or check with the licensing/procurement team if unsure).
2. Sign out of Office completely (File > Account > Sign Out) and sign back in with the correct account.
3. Go to File > Account and click 'Update License' or 'Activate Product' if the option is present.
4. Confirm the laptop's date and time are correct, as activation checks can fail with an incorrect system clock.
5. Run the Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant (SaRA) tool for Office activation issues if available via the Software Portal.
6. Restart the laptop after confirming license assignment and re-signing in, then relaunch Office.
7. Escalate to the M365 licensing team if the license is confirmed assigned in the admin center but activation still fails after sign-out/sign-in.

Affected Systems: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Document Sharing Link Not Working for External User
content:
Problem: A user shares a OneDrive or SharePoint document link with an external partner or client, but the recipient reports the link does not work or shows an access-denied message.

Symptoms:
- External recipient reports 'the link says I need permission' or 'the link doesn't work'
- Internal user confirms the link was generated and sent correctly
- Link may open fine for internal company users but fail specifically for external recipients
- Error for the recipient may reference needing to sign in or request access

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the link was generated with the correct sharing scope — 'Anyone with the link' or 'Specific people' including the external recipient's exact email address.
2. If 'Specific people' was used, confirm the external recipient is signing in with the exact email address the link was shared with.
3. Check whether external sharing is enabled for the specific SharePoint site or OneDrive tenant setting, as some sites restrict external sharing entirely.
4. Regenerate the sharing link and resend it, ensuring the correct permission level (view/edit) and audience are selected.
5. Ask the external recipient to check their spam/junk folder for an access request or verification code email tied to the guest sign-in process.
6. Verify the file/folder has not been moved or deleted since the link was generated, which would invalidate it.
7. Escalate to the SharePoint/M365 admin team if external sharing appears to be blocked at the tenant or site level and should be permitted for this scenario.

Affected Systems: OneDrive, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365, external/guest sharing
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: OneDrive and SharePoint Show Conflicting File Versions After Offline Editing
content:
Problem: After working offline and reconnecting, a user finds that OneDrive/SharePoint shows a different version of a file than what they edited, with their offline changes seemingly overwritten or missing.

Symptoms:
- File content after reconnecting does not match the changes made while offline
- User reports 'my changes are gone after I got back online' or 'it reverted to an old version'
- A conflict notification or duplicate file (with a device name suffix) may or may not have appeared
- Issue is more likely when the same file was also edited by another user or on another device during the offline period

Resolution Steps:
1. Check OneDrive/SharePoint version history (right-click the file > Version History) to locate the version containing the user's offline edits.
2. Restore the correct version from history if the current version does not reflect the expected changes.
3. Check the same folder for a duplicate conflict file (e.g., filename-ComputerName.docx) that may contain the offline edits separately.
4. If both versions have valuable content, manually merge the changes into a single correct file.
5. Explain to the user that simultaneous edits by multiple people/devices while offline can cause the last synced version to take precedence.
6. Recommend enabling 'Always keep on this device' for critical files that are frequently edited offline, and encourage reconnecting promptly after offline work.
7. Escalate to L2 if version history does not contain the expected offline changes at all, as this may indicate a sync failure that needs deeper investigation.

Affected Systems: OneDrive (Desktop), SharePoint Online, Word, Excel, Microsoft 365
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: User Forgot Password and Needs a Reset
content:
Problem: A user cannot remember their corporate account password and is unable to log into Windows, email, or other company systems that rely on the same credentials.

Symptoms:
- User reports 'I forgot my password' or 'I can't remember my login'
- Login attempts fail with 'incorrect password' across multiple systems using the same account
- User has not saved or written down the password anywhere accessible
- May be a new employee unfamiliar with the self-service reset process

Resolution Steps:
1. Direct the user to the self-service password reset (SSPR) portal if their account is enrolled, and confirm they have access to their registered MFA method.
2. If SSPR is unavailable or the user is not enrolled, verify the user's identity per company security policy before proceeding.
3. Perform an administrative password reset via the identity management console (Active Directory/Entra ID) if self-service is not possible.
4. Provide a secure temporary password through an approved secure channel, never via plain email or chat.
5. Instruct the user to change the temporary password immediately upon next login.
6. Confirm the user can successfully log into Windows and at least one other key system (e.g., email) after the reset.
7. Encourage enrollment in SSPR if not already enrolled, to reduce future reset turnaround time.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, Windows, Microsoft 365, enterprise applications
Category: Access / Authentication

title: Account Locked Out After Multiple Failed Login Attempts
content:
Problem: A user's account becomes locked after several consecutive failed login attempts, preventing sign-in even with the correct password until the lockout is cleared.

Symptoms:
- Login attempt shows 'Your account has been locked' or 'Account is temporarily locked'
- User confirms they are entering the correct password but access is still denied
- Lockout may have been triggered by a stale saved password on a mobile device or app after a recent password change
- User is unable to access any system tied to the same account

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the lockout reason in the identity management console (Active Directory/Entra ID sign-in logs) — repeated failed attempts, suspicious activity flag, etc.
2. Check for devices or applications (mobile mail app, mapped drives, old saved credentials) that may be repeatedly attempting login with an outdated password, causing the lockout.
3. Unlock the account through the appropriate admin console after verifying the user's identity.
4. Have the user update any cached/saved credentials on mobile devices, mapped network drives, or other apps to prevent immediate re-lockout.
5. If the account has a lockout policy with an automatic reset timer, inform the user of the expected wait time as an alternative to manual unlock.
6. Advise the user to change their password if a compromise is suspected, in coordination with the security team.
7. Escalate to the security team if the sign-in logs show lockout attempts from unfamiliar locations or devices, indicating possible account compromise.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, Windows, Microsoft 365
Category: Access / Authentication

title: Password Reset Link Expired or Not Received
content:
Problem: A user requests a password reset but either does not receive the reset email/link, or the link has expired by the time they attempt to use it.

Symptoms:
- User reports 'I never got the reset email' or 'the reset link says it's expired'
- Reset email may be delayed, filtered to spam, or sent to an outdated recovery email address
- Clicking an old link shows 'This link has expired' or 'Invalid or expired token'
- User may have multiple pending reset requests causing confusion about which link is valid

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the recovery email or phone number on file is current and accessible to the user.
2. Ask the user to check spam/junk folders for the reset email, as automated messages are sometimes filtered.
3. Have the user request a new reset link, since links are typically time-limited (commonly 15-60 minutes) and only the most recent one is usually valid.
4. Confirm the user is completing the reset promptly after receiving the email, rather than letting it sit unused.
5. If recovery contact information is outdated or inaccessible, verify identity per policy and update the recovery method through the appropriate admin console.
6. If self-service reset continues to fail after a fresh link and confirmed correct recovery info, perform an administrative reset instead.
7. Escalate to the identity team if reset emails are not being delivered system-wide, as this may indicate an email delivery or SSPR configuration issue.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, self-service password reset
Category: Access / Authentication

title: MFA Push Notification Not Received
content:
Problem: A user attempting to log in is expecting a multi-factor authentication (MFA) push notification on their phone, but it never arrives, blocking access to the requested system.

Symptoms:
- Login screen shows 'Waiting for approval' but no notification appears on the user's phone
- User reports 'I'm not getting the MFA push' or 'the approval notification never shows up'
- Phone has normal connectivity and the authenticator app opens without error
- May occur only on certain networks (e.g., poor cellular signal) or be intermittent

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the user's phone has an active internet connection (Wi-Fi or cellular data) and the authenticator app is updated to the latest version.
2. Have the user manually open the authenticator app to check for a pending request, since notifications can sometimes fail to display even when the request exists.
3. Check that push notifications are enabled for the authenticator app in the phone's OS-level notification settings.
4. Have the user retry the login attempt to generate a new push request, as the previous one may have expired.
5. If push consistently fails, have the user switch to an alternate MFA method (e.g., time-based one-time code) if enrolled.
6. Confirm the correct phone number/device is registered for MFA in the identity portal, in case an old device is still receiving requests.
7. Escalate to the identity team if push notifications fail consistently across attempts and devices, as it may indicate an MFA service issue.

Affected Systems: Microsoft Authenticator, Entra ID MFA, enterprise SSO
Category: Access / MFA

title: MFA Code Rejected / 'Invalid Verification Code'
content:
Problem: A user enters the one-time verification code from their authenticator app or SMS, but the system rejects it as invalid, preventing successful login.

Symptoms:
- Error message reads 'Invalid verification code' or 'The code you entered is incorrect'
- User confirms they are copying the code correctly from the authenticator app
- Code may be accepted on retry after waiting for the next code cycle
- User reports 'my MFA code keeps saying it's wrong'

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the code is being entered before it expires; time-based codes typically refresh every 30-60 seconds.
2. Check that the device's date and time are set to automatic/correct, as a clock drift on the phone commonly causes valid codes to be rejected.
3. Have the user wait for the authenticator app to generate a completely new code and try again, rather than reusing a code close to expiration.
4. If using SMS-based codes, confirm the message was received promptly and not delayed due to carrier issues.
5. Verify the user is using the correct account entry within the authenticator app if multiple accounts are registered.
6. If codes consistently fail even when freshly generated, consider re-registering the MFA method in the identity portal.
7. Escalate to the identity team if code rejection continues after confirming device time sync and fresh code entry.

Affected Systems: Microsoft Authenticator, Entra ID MFA, SMS-based MFA
Category: Access / MFA

title: Lost or Replaced Phone / No Access to MFA Authenticator App
content:
Problem: A user has lost, replaced, or reset their mobile phone and no longer has access to their MFA authenticator app, blocking them from completing sign-in to any MFA-protected system.

Symptoms:
- User cannot complete MFA because the registered device/app no longer exists or was wiped
- User reports 'I got a new phone and lost my authenticator' or 'my phone was lost/stolen'
- No backup MFA method is available or the user does not recall setting one up
- User is completely locked out of all systems requiring MFA

Resolution Steps:
1. Verify the user's identity thoroughly per company security policy before proceeding, since this scenario is a common social engineering target.
2. Check if the user has an alternate registered MFA method (backup phone number, backup codes) that can be used instead.
3. If a security incident is suspected (phone stolen rather than simply replaced), coordinate immediately with the security team before any MFA reset.
4. Once identity is confirmed, reset/remove the old MFA method in the identity portal (Entra ID) to allow re-registration.
5. Guide the user through re-registering MFA on their new device using the standard enrollment process.
6. Confirm successful login with the newly registered MFA method before closing the ticket.
7. Document the identity verification steps taken in the ticket for audit purposes, per security policy.

Edge Case: If the phone was stolen or compromised, treat this as a potential security incident and involve the security team before resetting MFA, since resetting hastily could allow an attacker to register their own device.

Affected Systems: Entra ID MFA, Microsoft Authenticator, enterprise SSO
Category: Access / MFA

title: User Cannot Register for MFA / Setup Fails
content:
Problem: A user attempting to enroll in multi-factor authentication for the first time encounters an error or is unable to complete the setup process, such as scanning a QR code or verifying a phone number.

Symptoms:
- QR code scan in the authenticator app fails or the app shows 'Something went wrong'
- Phone number verification code for MFA setup never arrives
- User reports 'I can't finish setting up MFA' or 'the setup process is stuck'
- Setup may be required before the user can access any company systems for the first time (new hire scenario)

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the user is using the correct, currently supported authenticator app (e.g., Microsoft Authenticator) rather than an unsupported third-party app.
2. Have the user ensure their phone's camera has permission to scan QR codes, or manually enter the setup key/code if scanning fails.
3. Confirm the mobile device has an active internet connection during setup, as registration requires real-time communication with the identity service.
4. If using SMS verification, confirm the phone number entered is correct and can receive texts (no carrier blocks on short codes).
5. Clear the browser cache or try the enrollment process in a different browser/incognito window if the enrollment page itself is malfunctioning.
6. Restart the enrollment process from the beginning rather than attempting to resume a partially completed setup, which can sometimes cause conflicts.
7. Escalate to the identity team if enrollment fails consistently across devices and browsers, as it may indicate a tenant-level MFA configuration issue.

Affected Systems: Entra ID MFA, Microsoft Authenticator, new hire onboarding
Category: Access / MFA

title: SSO Login Redirect Loop / Stuck on Loading Screen
content:
Problem: A user attempting to log into an application via Single Sign-On is caught in a continuous redirect loop between the application and the identity provider, or the page hangs indefinitely on a loading screen.

Symptoms:
- Browser URL bar shows repeated redirects between the app and the SSO/identity provider login page
- Page may hang on a blank or spinning loading screen without ever reaching the application
- User reports 'it just keeps redirecting me' or 'the login page never finishes loading'
- Issue may be specific to one browser or resolve temporarily in an incognito window

Resolution Steps:
1. Clear the browser's cache and cookies for both the application's domain and the identity provider's domain.
2. Try the same login in an incognito/private browsing window to rule out a corrupted session or conflicting cached token.
3. Confirm the user is not signed into multiple company or personal accounts simultaneously in the same browser, which can cause identity conflicts.
4. Try a different supported browser to determine if the issue is browser-specific.
5. Check the system date and time for accuracy, as token validation can fail with an incorrect clock, contributing to redirect loops.
6. Confirm with the application owner or identity team whether the SSO configuration (e.g., SAML/OIDC settings) for this specific application was recently changed.
7. Escalate to the identity/SSO team with the exact application name and browser used if the loop persists after cache clearing and testing in incognito mode.

Affected Systems: Entra ID SSO, SAML, OIDC, enterprise applications
Category: Access / SSO

title: 'Access Denied' Error Logging Into Enterprise Application via SSO
content:
Problem: A user successfully authenticates through the company's SSO identity provider but receives an 'Access Denied' or 'You do not have permission to access this application' error afterward.

Symptoms:
- SSO authentication completes successfully (user sees their identity provider login succeed), but the target application then denies access
- Error message reads 'Access Denied', 'Unauthorized', or 'You are not assigned to this application'
- User may be a new hire, recent transfer, or someone whose role recently changed
- Other SSO-enabled applications may work fine for the same user

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the user has actually been assigned/licensed for this specific application in the identity provider's enterprise application settings.
2. Check whether the user belongs to the correct security group required for access to this application, as many SSO apps gate access via group membership.
3. If access should exist based on role, submit or verify an access request through the standard application access process.
4. Allow time for recent group membership changes to propagate, as this can take anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours depending on sync schedules.
5. Have the user sign out completely and sign back in after any group/assignment change to refresh their authentication token with updated permissions.
6. Test in an incognito window to rule out a stale cached token issue separate from actual permission assignment.
7. Escalate to the application owner or identity team if the user is confirmed to have appropriate group membership/assignment but access is still denied.

Affected Systems: Entra ID SSO, enterprise applications, SAML/OIDC applications
Category: Access / SSO

title: Application Login Fails With Valid Credentials (Non-SSO Application)
content:
Problem: A user cannot log into a specific business application that uses its own independent login (not integrated with company SSO), despite entering credentials they believe are correct.

Symptoms:
- Application shows 'Invalid username or password' despite the user being confident in their credentials
- Credentials work correctly for other, unrelated systems (ruling out a general password issue)
- User reports 'I can log into everything else but not into [specific application]'
- May follow a recent password change that was not updated within the standalone application

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm this application uses its own separate credential store rather than SSO, since standalone apps do not automatically pick up company password changes.
2. Verify the exact username format required by the application (e.g., email vs. a separate application-specific username).
3. If the user's company password was recently changed, check whether the application requires a manual credential update, and update it if the user has that capability.
4. Use the application's own 'Forgot Password' feature if available, since this is separate from the company SSPR process.
5. Confirm the application account is not locked or disabled independently of the user's main company account.
6. Check with the application owner/admin whether the account is provisioned correctly and active on their end.
7. Escalate to the application owner or vendor support if credentials are confirmed correct and active but login still fails.

Affected Systems: Standalone/non-SSO business applications
Category: Access / Authentication

title: Session Expires Too Quickly / User Frequently Logged Out
content:
Problem: A user is repeatedly logged out of an application or system after a short period, well before the expected session duration, disrupting their workflow throughout the day.

Symptoms:
- User is prompted to log in again every 10-20 minutes despite active use
- User reports 'I keep getting logged out' or 'my session doesn't last very long'
- Issue may be specific to one application or browser, or occur system-wide
- May correlate with recent browser updates, extension installs, or security policy changes

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm whether the short session duration is expected behavior per the application's or company's security policy (some sensitive apps intentionally use short sessions).
2. Check if the browser is set to clear cookies on close or has an aggressive privacy/tracking prevention setting that may be clearing session tokens.
3. Test in a different browser to determine whether the issue is browser-specific.
4. Check for browser extensions (ad blockers, privacy tools) that may be interfering with session cookies, and disable them temporarily to test.
5. Confirm the system date and time are accurate, as clock drift can cause tokens to appear expired prematurely.
6. If the issue is specific to one application, check with the application owner whether a recent session-timeout policy change was made.
7. Escalate to the identity/security team if session length is shorter than the documented policy and not explained by browser settings.

Affected Systems: Entra ID SSO, enterprise applications, web browsers
Category: Access / Authentication

title: User Has No Access to Required Folder or Application (Permission Denied)
content:
Problem: A user attempts to open a network folder, shared drive, or internal application they need for their role, and receives a permission-denied error despite believing they should have access.

Symptoms:
- Error reads 'Access is denied' or 'You don't have permission to access this folder'
- User states this is needed for their current role/project and expects access
- May be a new hire, recent transfer, or someone whose responsibilities recently changed
- Other, unrelated folders/applications may be accessible normally

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the exact resource (folder path, application name) the user needs access to, and the specific access level (read, write, admin).
2. Check whether the user has an approved access request on file, or whether this is a new request that needs to be submitted.
3. If access should already exist, verify the user's current security group memberships against those required for the resource.
4. If a request is needed, submit or guide the user through the standard access request/approval process, including required manager or resource-owner sign-off.
5. For newly granted access, inform the user that propagation may take some time and advise them to sign out and back in before retrying.
6. Confirm the user is attempting access from an expected device/network, as some resources are additionally restricted by location or device compliance.
7. Escalate to the resource owner or access management team if access is confirmed granted but the permission error persists.

Affected Systems: File shares, Active Directory, enterprise applications
Category: Access / Permissions

title: Conditional Access Blocking Sign-In (Untrusted Device or Location)
content:
Problem: A user is blocked from signing in due to the organization's conditional access policies, typically triggered by signing in from an unmanaged device, unfamiliar location, or non-compliant device state.

Symptoms:
- Sign-in attempt shows a message such as 'Your sign-in was blocked' or 'This device does not meet the requirements set by your organization'
- User may be traveling, using a personal device, or connecting from a new network
- Message may specifically reference device compliance, location, or an unsupported browser/app
- Credentials and MFA are entered correctly but access is still blocked at this final step

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm whether the user is attempting to sign in from a company-managed device or a personal/unmanaged device, as this is a common trigger.
2. If on a personal device, direct the user to a compliant company-managed device where possible, or to the approved BYOD access path if one exists.
3. If on a company device, confirm the device shows as compliant in the endpoint management console (e.g., Intune) — check for pending compliance policy issues like outdated OS or missing encryption.
4. If travel or new location triggered the block, confirm with the security team whether this is expected policy behavior (e.g., blocking sign-ins from certain countries) versus something to be adjusted.
5. Check the sign-in logs in the identity portal for the specific conditional access policy that triggered the block, to understand the exact requirement not being met.
6. Do not attempt to bypass conditional access policies; escalate to the security/identity team for any policy exception requests.
7. Document the specific blocking policy and circumstances in the ticket when escalating for a possible exception or device remediation.

Affected Systems: Entra ID Conditional Access, Intune, enterprise applications
Category: Access / Conditional Access

title: Password Reset Fails Despite Correct Identity Verification
content:
Problem: A user completes the identity verification steps for a self-service password reset (security questions, MFA, etc.) but the reset process fails to complete or errors out before a new password can be set.

Symptoms:
- SSPR flow completes verification successfully but then shows an error at the final 'set new password' step
- New password entered is rejected repeatedly even when it appears to meet complexity requirements
- User reports 'I did everything right but it still won't let me reset my password'
- Process may work in one browser but fail in another

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the new password meets the organization's actual complexity requirements (length, character types, and that it does not match recent password history).
2. Try the reset process in a different browser or incognito window in case of a stuck session or cached form data.
3. Confirm the account is not simultaneously flagged for a security hold or investigation that would block a self-service reset.
4. Check if the user is attempting to reuse a recent previous password, which is commonly blocked by password history policy.
5. Have the user restart the SSPR process from the beginning rather than continuing a stalled session.
6. If the error is consistent and not explained by password policy, perform an administrative password reset instead after identity verification.
7. Escalate to the identity team with the exact error message if SSPR consistently fails at the final step for this user despite meeting all requirements.

Affected Systems: Entra ID, self-service password reset, Active Directory
Category: Access / Authentication

title: New Hire Has No System Access / Account Not Provisioned
content:
Problem: A new employee's start date has arrived but they have no working account, email, or access to any required systems, indicating the provisioning process did not complete.

Symptoms:
- New hire cannot log into their laptop, email, or any assigned application on their first day
- No account appears to exist in Active Directory/Entra ID when searched by name
- User reports being told to start but 'nothing works' or 'I have no login at all'
- May be caused by a delayed or incomplete HR-to-IT provisioning workflow

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm with HR that the new hire's start date and employment status are correctly recorded in the HR system that triggers provisioning.
2. Check the identity management console (Active Directory/Entra ID) to see if an account exists but is simply not yet enabled, versus not created at all.
3. If an account exists but is disabled/pending, work with the onboarding/identity team to activate it per standard procedure.
4. If no account exists at all, escalate immediately to the identity/provisioning team as a priority onboarding issue, since the employee cannot begin work.
5. Once provisioned, confirm the account has the correct baseline access (email, core applications) assigned per the new hire's role/department.
6. Verify the new hire can successfully log into their laptop and at least email before considering the issue resolved.
7. Document any gaps in the provisioning workflow (e.g., missing manager approval) that caused the delay, for process improvement.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, HR provisioning systems, Microsoft 365
Category: Access / Provisioning

title: Departing Employee Access Revocation Request
content:
Problem: An employee is departing the company (resignation, termination, or contract end), and their system access needs to be promptly and completely revoked per offboarding policy.

Symptoms:
- HR or a manager submits an offboarding/termination notice requiring access removal
- Request may specify an immediate revocation (involuntary) or an end-of-day/end-of-notice-period revocation (voluntary)
- Access spans multiple systems: Windows account, email, VPN, SSO applications, shared mailboxes, and physical access where applicable
- Time-sensitive request, particularly for involuntary departures

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the exact revocation timing required (immediate vs. scheduled) and the authorization source (HR, manager, security team) per company offboarding policy.
2. Disable the user's Active Directory/Entra ID account, which will cascade to block most SSO-integrated application access.
3. Revoke active sessions and refresh tokens for the account to immediately terminate any already-logged-in sessions, not just block future logins.
4. Remove or disable VPN access specifically, as VPN sessions may not always be terminated solely by disabling the primary account.
5. Forward or reassign the departing employee's mailbox per data retention policy, and remove them from any shared mailboxes and distribution lists.
6. Notify the asset management team to arrange return/wipe of company hardware (laptop, phone, access badge) per standard offboarding procedure.
7. Confirm with the requester (HR/manager) once all revocation steps are complete, and document the completion timestamp in the ticket.

Edge Case: For involuntary/high-risk terminations, prioritize immediate account disablement and session revocation above all other offboarding steps, and coordinate closely with security and HR on timing.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, Microsoft 365, VPN, enterprise applications
Category: Access / Deprovisioning

title: Shared or Service Account Login Issues
content:
Problem: A shared team account or automated service account fails to log in or authenticate, affecting a process, application, or team function that depends on it rather than a single individual user.

Symptoms:
- Service account authentication fails, causing an automated process or integration to stop working
- Shared team account (e.g., a departmental mailbox login) is rejected by the login system
- Error may reference an expired password, disabled account, or MFA requirement unexpectedly being enforced on a service account
- Multiple team members or an automated system are affected simultaneously rather than a single individual

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm which specific shared or service account is affected and what process/team depends on it.
2. Check the account's status (enabled/disabled, password expiration) in Active Directory/Entra ID, as service accounts sometimes have separate password expiration policies.
3. Confirm whether MFA is correctly configured (typically MFA should be exempted or specially handled for true service accounts per policy) and not blocking automated logins unexpectedly.
4. Identify the account owner/steward on record for this shared or service account to coordinate any password reset, since resets can break dependent integrations if not communicated.
5. If a password reset is required, coordinate with all known consumers of the account (scripts, integrations, team members) to update credentials simultaneously.
6. Test the account login/authentication in isolation after any change before considering the issue resolved.
7. Escalate to the identity/security team if the account's policy configuration (MFA, expiration) appears incorrect for a service/shared account type.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, service accounts, shared mailboxes
Category: Access / Authentication

title: SSO Not Recognizing Correct Identity Provider / Wrong Tenant
content:
Problem: A user attempting SSO login is redirected to an unexpected identity provider login page, a personal Microsoft account prompt, or the wrong company tenant, rather than the correct corporate identity provider.

Symptoms:
- User is prompted with a personal Microsoft/Google account login instead of the corporate SSO page
- User reports 'it's asking me to log in with my personal account' or 'it went to the wrong company login'
- May occur if the user has multiple Microsoft/Google accounts signed into the same browser
- Entering corporate credentials at the wrong prompt results in an error or unrelated account access

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm which accounts are currently signed into the browser (e.g., via the account picker/profile icon) and identify if a personal account is being defaulted to.
2. Have the user sign out of all accounts in the browser, or use an incognito/private window to start with a clean session.
3. Ensure the user selects 'Use another account' or manually enters their full corporate email address rather than relying on a cached/default account suggestion.
4. If using a browser profile, confirm the user is in their work-managed browser profile rather than a personal profile, if the organization uses browser profile separation.
5. Clear cookies for the specific identity provider domain if the wrong-tenant redirect persists even after choosing the correct account.
6. Confirm the application's SSO configuration is pointed to the correct tenant if this issue affects multiple users on the same application.
7. Escalate to the identity/SSO team if the application is consistently misconfigured to point to the wrong tenant or identity provider.

Affected Systems: Entra ID SSO, Google Workspace SSO, enterprise applications
Category: Access / SSO

title: User Locked Out of VPN or Enterprise App Due to Expired Certificate
content:
Problem: A user is unable to authenticate to the VPN or a certificate-based enterprise application because their client authentication certificate has expired, and simple password/MFA retries do not resolve it.

Symptoms:
- VPN or application login fails with a certificate-related error, such as 'certificate has expired' or 'no valid certificate found'
- Issue often appears suddenly for a user who previously connected without issue
- User's password and MFA are confirmed correct and not the cause
- May affect several users at once if certificates were issued in the same batch and expire around the same time

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the exact certificate error message and which application/service is reporting it.
2. Check the device's certificate store (certmgr.msc) for the relevant client certificate and review its expiration date.
3. If expired, confirm whether the device is enrolled in automatic certificate renewal (common with domain-joined or Intune-managed devices) and whether renewal has simply not yet triggered.
4. Trigger a manual sync/check-in with the device management platform (e.g., Intune) to prompt certificate renewal if supported.
5. If automatic renewal does not resolve it, this typically requires re-enrollment of the device with the certificate authority — escalate to the endpoint/identity management team.
6. Advise the user of expected downtime while the certificate is reissued, and confirm successful VPN/application login once complete.
7. Escalate to L2/PKI team if multiple users are affected simultaneously, as it may indicate a batch of certificates nearing expiration that requires proactive renewal.

Affected Systems: VPN clients, certificate-based authentication, Intune, PKI
Category: Access / Authentication

Diagnostic Integration: Run internal diagnostic tool 'vpn_check' to verify gateway reachability, IP lease allocation, and tunnel connectivity for target device.

title: Duplicate or Conflicting User Accounts Preventing Login
content:
Problem: A user has two or more accounts associated with their identity (e.g., from a rehire, name change, or merger), causing login confusion, incorrect access, or outright login failures.

Symptoms:
- User has two different usernames/emails and is unsure which to use, or logins fail intermittently depending on which is tried
- Access to resources is inconsistent — available under one account but not the other
- Situation often follows a rehire, department transfer combined with a system migration, or company merger/acquisition
- User reports 'I think I have two accounts and I don't know which one to use'

Resolution Steps:
1. Search the identity management console (Active Directory/Entra ID) for all accounts associated with the user's name or known email addresses.
2. Determine which account is the current, active, authoritative account per HR records (typically the most recently provisioned one tied to current employment).
3. Confirm with HR/identity governance which account should be retained and which should be disabled or merged, as this decision should not be made unilaterally by L1.
4. Once the correct account is identified, direct the user to use only that account going forward and update any bookmarks/saved logins accordingly.
5. Coordinate with the identity governance team to properly disable or merge the duplicate account to prevent future confusion.
6. Verify the user's access, mailbox, and files are correctly associated with the retained account before the duplicate is fully disabled.
7. Escalate to the identity governance team for the formal account merge/cleanup process, as this typically falls outside standard L1 scope.

Affected Systems: Active Directory, Entra ID, Microsoft 365
Category: Access / Authentication

title: External Monitor Not Detected When Connected
content:
Problem: A user connects an external monitor to their laptop, but the display is not detected and only the laptop's built-in screen shows an image.

Symptoms:
- External monitor remains blank/black or shows 'No Signal' after connecting
- Windows Display Settings does not list the second monitor as an available display
- User reports 'my monitor isn't being detected' or 'the second screen isn't showing up'
- Monitor works fine when tested with a different laptop or source

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the monitor is powered on and set to the correct input source (HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C) matching the cable used.
2. Press Windows key + P to open the display/project menu and confirm 'Extend' or 'Duplicate' is selected rather than 'PC screen only'.
3. Try a different cable and port on both the laptop and the monitor to rule out a faulty cable or port.
4. Click 'Detect' in Settings > System > Display if the monitor still does not appear automatically.
5. Update the graphics driver via Device Manager or the manufacturer's site, especially after a recent Windows Update.
6. If connecting through a dock or adapter, test connecting the monitor directly to the laptop to isolate whether the dock/adapter is the cause.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the monitor and laptop model if the display is still not detected after testing a direct connection and updated drivers.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, external monitors, HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C
Category: Hardware / Display

title: External Monitor Flickering or Incorrect Resolution
content:
Problem: An external monitor connected to a laptop displays a flickering image, incorrect/blurry resolution, or an unusual refresh rate compared to its native specifications.

Symptoms:
- Screen flickers intermittently or shows visible screen tearing
- Text and icons appear blurry, oversized, or stretched incorrectly
- User reports 'my monitor keeps flickering' or 'the resolution looks wrong'
- Issue may worsen when the laptop is on battery power versus plugged in

Resolution Steps:
1. Go to Settings > System > Display and confirm the resolution matches the monitor's native/recommended resolution.
2. Check and set the correct refresh rate under Settings > System > Display > Advanced display settings.
3. Try a different video cable, as flickering is commonly caused by a damaged or poor-quality HDMI/DisplayPort cable.
4. Update the graphics driver to the latest version from the manufacturer.
5. Test the monitor on a different port (e.g., DisplayPort instead of HDMI) if multiple port types are available on both devices.
6. Check the laptop's power plan settings, as some power-saving modes can reduce refresh rate/performance to external displays on battery.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if flickering continues after cable, driver, and resolution checks, as it may indicate a failing monitor or GPU output.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, external monitors
Category: Hardware / Display

title: Docking Station Not Detecting Laptop / Peripherals Not Working
content:
Problem: A laptop connected to a docking station does not recognize the dock at all, and none of the connected peripherals (monitors, keyboard, mouse, Ethernet) function.

Symptoms:
- No peripherals connected via the dock respond, as if the dock is not connected at all
- Dock's power/status LED may be off or showing an error color
- User reports 'my dock isn't working' or 'nothing works when I plug into the dock'
- Laptop may charge through the dock but show no other functionality, or not charge at all

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the dock is receiving power (check the dock's power LED and power adapter connection).
2. Disconnect and firmly reconnect the laptop's connection cable (USB-C/Thunderbolt) to the dock.
3. Try a different port on the laptop if multiple USB-C/Thunderbolt ports are available.
4. Restart the laptop with the dock connected, as some docks require a fresh boot to initialize properly.
5. Check Device Manager for the docking station listed as a USB device, and update its driver if an error icon is present.
6. Test the dock with a different laptop, or test the laptop with a different dock, to isolate whether the dock or laptop is at fault.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the dock model and laptop model if the dock remains unresponsive after basic reconnection and driver checks.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, USB-C docking stations, Thunderbolt docking stations
Category: Hardware / Docking Station

title: Docking Station External Displays Not Working
content:
Problem: A laptop connects successfully to a docking station (charging and USB peripherals work), but external monitors connected through the dock show no signal.

Symptoms:
- Dock is detected and other peripherals (keyboard, mouse, Ethernet) function normally
- External monitor(s) connected via the dock show 'No Signal' or remain blank
- User reports 'everything works through the dock except my monitor'
- Monitor may work fine when connected directly to the laptop instead of through the dock

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the monitor works when connected directly to the laptop, to isolate the dock as the likely cause.
2. Check that the correct video port on the dock is being used (some docks have both DisplayPort and HDMI with different capabilities).
3. Update the dock's driver/firmware via the manufacturer's utility or the internal Software Portal.
4. Restart the laptop with the dock and monitor connected to force redetection.
5. Check Settings > System > Display and click 'Detect' to manually search for the connected display.
6. If using multiple monitors through the dock, confirm the dock and laptop's GPU support the number of displays and resolution combination being attempted (some docks have limits).
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the dock and monitor model if the display still fails after firmware updates and testing a direct connection.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, docking stations, external monitors
Category: Hardware / Docking Station

title: Keyboard Not Responding or Certain Keys Not Working
content:
Problem: A keyboard (built-in or external) does not respond at all to input, or specific keys fail to register while others work normally.

Symptoms:
- No keys respond when typing, or only certain keys (e.g., a full row or specific characters) fail to work
- User reports 'my keyboard stopped working' or 'some keys don't type anything'
- Issue may be intermittent, worsening with certain applications or specific typing patterns
- External keyboard may work fine on another device, isolating the issue to this laptop

Resolution Steps:
1. For external keyboards, unplug and reconnect the USB cable or re-pair if wireless, checking/replacing batteries if applicable.
2. Test the keyboard in a different USB port, or with a different laptop, to isolate whether the keyboard or the laptop is at fault.
3. For built-in laptop keyboards, restart the laptop, as a stuck keyboard driver state can sometimes cause this.
4. Check Device Manager for the keyboard listed with an error icon, and update or reinstall the driver if present.
5. Confirm no Sticky Keys, Filter Keys, or other accessibility settings (Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard) are inadvertently altering key behavior.
6. Clean visible debris from under affected keys if only specific physical keys are failing on a built-in keyboard.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if specific keys consistently fail on the built-in keyboard, as this typically indicates a physical hardware fault requiring repair.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, built-in laptop keyboards, external keyboards
Category: Hardware / Peripherals

title: Wireless Keyboard or Mouse Not Pairing or Connecting
content:
Problem: A wireless (Bluetooth or USB dongle-based) keyboard or mouse fails to pair with the laptop, or was previously paired but no longer connects.

Symptoms:
- Device does not appear in the Bluetooth device list when attempting to pair
- Previously paired device shows as 'Connected' in settings but does not respond
- User reports 'my wireless mouse/keyboard won't connect' or 'it just stopped working'
- Device works fine when tested with a different computer

Resolution Steps:
1. Check and replace batteries in the wireless keyboard/mouse, as low battery is the most common cause of connectivity issues.
2. For USB dongle-based devices, unplug and reconnect the dongle in a different USB port.
3. For Bluetooth devices, remove the device from Settings > Bluetooth & devices and re-pair it from scratch.
4. Confirm the device is in pairing mode (typically via a dedicated button) before attempting to connect from the laptop.
5. Restart the laptop's Bluetooth adapter by toggling Bluetooth off and on in Settings.
6. Move any other wireless devices (other Bluetooth peripherals, Wi-Fi routers) away temporarily to rule out interference.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the device model if pairing consistently fails after battery replacement and re-pairing attempts.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, Bluetooth peripherals, wireless keyboards, wireless mice
Category: Hardware / Peripherals

title: Mouse Cursor Freezing or Lagging
content:
Problem: The mouse cursor moves erratically, freezes intermittently, or lags noticeably behind physical mouse movement, whether using a wired, wireless, or trackpad input.

Symptoms:
- Cursor movement is jumpy, delayed, or occasionally freezes for a few seconds
- User reports 'my mouse is lagging' or 'the cursor keeps freezing'
- Issue may be worse over Wi-Fi/Bluetooth (wireless mice) or correlate with high CPU usage
- Physical mouse movement resumes cursor tracking after the freeze without needing to reconnect

Resolution Steps:
1. Check Task Manager for high CPU or disk usage that may be causing general system lag affecting cursor responsiveness.
2. For wireless mice, replace the batteries and ensure a clear line of sight/minimal distance to the receiver or Bluetooth adapter.
3. Test the mouse on a different surface, as certain surfaces (glass, highly reflective) can interfere with optical/laser tracking.
4. Update the mouse driver via Device Manager, particularly for gaming or specialty mice with custom drivers.
5. Disable mouse pointer enhancement features (Control Panel > Mouse > Pointer Options > uncheck 'Enhance pointer precision') to test if this is contributing.
6. Test with a different mouse to isolate whether the issue is the mouse hardware or the laptop/USB port.
7. Escalate to L2 if lag persists across mice and correlates with no other system performance issues, as it may point to a USB controller or driver-level issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, wired mice, wireless mice, trackpads
Category: Hardware / Peripherals

title: Webcam Not Detected or Not Working
content:
Problem: A laptop's built-in or external webcam is not detected by Windows or applications, preventing video from being used in any application, not just a single meeting tool.

Symptoms:
- Camera does not appear as an option in any application's video device list
- Windows Camera app shows an error such as 'We can't find your camera'
- User reports 'my webcam isn't working anywhere' or 'no camera is detected at all'
- Camera indicator light (if present) does not illuminate when applications attempt to access it

Resolution Steps:
1. Check Windows privacy settings (Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera) to confirm camera access is enabled for apps generally and for the specific application in use.
2. Open Device Manager and check under Cameras/Imaging devices for the webcam; if missing or showing an error, update or reinstall the driver.
3. For external webcams, disconnect and reconnect the USB cable, testing a different USB port.
4. Restart the laptop to clear any stuck camera process or driver state.
5. Test the camera in the built-in Windows Camera app to isolate whether the issue is system-wide or application-specific.
6. Check if antivirus/endpoint security software has a camera-blocking feature that may be inadvertently restricting access.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the webcam model if the camera remains undetected after driver updates and privacy setting checks, as it may indicate a hardware failure.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, built-in webcams, external webcams
Category: Hardware / Webcam

title: Webcam Image Blurry, Dark, or Low Quality
content:
Problem: A webcam is detected and functioning, but the video image quality is notably blurry, too dark, grainy, or otherwise degraded compared to normal expected quality.

Symptoms:
- Video image appears out of focus, dim, or pixelated during calls or recordings
- User reports 'my camera looks blurry' or 'the video quality is really bad'
- Issue may worsen in low-light environments or with backlighting
- Other participants in a call comment on poor video quality

Resolution Steps:
1. Clean the camera lens with a soft, dry cloth, as smudges are a very common cause of blurry video.
2. Check the lighting in the user's environment; recommend facing a light source rather than having it behind them to reduce darkness/backlighting issues.
3. Adjust camera settings (brightness, contrast) within the application or Windows Camera settings if available.
4. Confirm the webcam driver is up to date via Device Manager or manufacturer utility.
5. Check the application's video quality/resolution setting, as some apps default to lower quality to conserve bandwidth.
6. Test the camera in the Windows Camera app to determine if the quality issue is consistent across all applications or specific to one.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the webcam model if image quality remains poor after cleaning, lighting adjustment, and driver updates, as it may indicate a hardware defect.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, built-in webcams, external webcams
Category: Hardware / Webcam

title: Microphone Not Detected or Not Picking Up Sound
content:
Problem: A microphone (built-in, headset, or standalone) is either not recognized by Windows/applications, or is recognized but does not pick up any sound when the user speaks.

Symptoms:
- Microphone does not appear in the device list, or shows as connected but with no input level movement when speaking
- User reports 'my mic isn't picking up anything' or 'people can't hear me at all'
- Sound settings input test/level meter shows no activity despite speaking into the microphone
- Issue may be specific to one application while others detect the mic correctly

Resolution Steps:
1. Check Windows Sound settings (Settings > System > Sound > Input) to confirm the correct microphone is selected as the default input device.
2. Speak into the microphone while viewing the input level meter in Sound settings to confirm whether any signal is detected at the system level.
3. Confirm microphone privacy permissions are enabled (Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone) for both apps generally and the specific application.
4. Check for a physical mute switch or button on the microphone/headset that may be engaged.
5. For USB microphones, disconnect and reconnect to a different USB port; for 3.5mm headsets, ensure the plug is fully seated.
6. Update the audio driver via Device Manager, particularly if the mic previously worked and stopped after a Windows Update.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the microphone/headset model if no input is detected at the system level after driver updates and permission checks.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, built-in microphones, USB microphones, headsets
Category: Hardware / Audio

title: Headset Audio Not Working / One-Sided Sound
content:
Problem: A headset produces no sound at all, or sound is only heard in one ear, despite the headset appearing connected and selected as the active audio device.

Symptoms:
- No audio plays through the headset despite it being selected as the output device
- Sound is heard in only the left or right ear, not both
- User reports 'my headset isn't working' or 'I can only hear out of one side'
- Issue may be specific to the headset while laptop speakers work normally

Resolution Steps:
1. Check the balance setting in Windows Sound settings (Settings > System > Sound > Volume mixer, or Control Panel > Sound > Playback > Properties > Levels/Balance) for one-sided audio.
2. Confirm the headset is fully and correctly seated in its port (3.5mm jack) or properly connected/paired (USB or Bluetooth).
3. Test the headset on a different device (phone, another laptop) to determine if the headset itself is faulty.
4. For 3.5mm headsets, gently wiggle the connector while listening for audio changes, which can indicate a damaged jack or connector.
5. Update the audio driver via Device Manager, especially if the issue began after a Windows Update.
6. For Bluetooth headsets, remove and re-pair the device to rule out a corrupted pairing profile.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the headset model if audio issues persist after testing on another device and updating drivers, as it may indicate a physical hardware fault.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, wired headsets, Bluetooth headsets, USB headsets
Category: Hardware / Audio

title: Laptop Speakers Not Producing Sound
content:
Problem: A laptop's built-in speakers produce no sound at all, despite the volume being turned up and no headset or external speaker connected.

Symptoms:
- No sound plays from the laptop's built-in speakers for any application or system sound
- Volume icon in the system tray may show as muted or at zero even after adjustment
- User reports 'my laptop has no sound' or 'the speakers stopped working'
- Sound may work correctly through a headset or external speaker plugged into the same laptop

Resolution Steps:
1. Check the system volume level and mute status via the taskbar volume icon, ensuring it is not muted or set to zero.
2. Confirm the correct output device (laptop speakers, not a disconnected external device) is selected in Settings > System > Sound > Output.
3. Play a test sound (Settings > System > Sound > Output > Test) to confirm whether any output is detected at all.
4. Restart the Windows Audio service via services.msc if no test sound plays.
5. Update the audio driver via Device Manager, particularly after a recent Windows Update.
6. Check for a physical mute key on the keyboard that may have been accidentally pressed.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if no sound plays from built-in speakers after driver updates and service restart, as it may indicate a hardware failure.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, built-in laptop speakers
Category: Hardware / Audio

title: Printer Not Detected or Cannot Be Added
content:
Problem: A user is unable to add a network or USB printer to their laptop, or a previously working printer no longer appears in the device list.

Symptoms:
- Printer does not appear when searching via Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > Add device
- Error such as 'Windows cannot connect to the printer' appears when attempting to add it manually
- User reports 'I can't add the printer' or 'my printer disappeared from the list'
- Other users/devices on the same network can successfully print to the same printer

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the printer is powered on and connected to the network (check its display panel or status lights for connectivity).
2. For network printers, confirm the laptop is on the same network/VLAN as the printer, especially relevant for VPN-connected or guest network users.
3. Try adding the printer using its known IP address directly (Add printer > The printer that I want isn't listed > Add using IP address) rather than relying on network discovery.
4. Restart the Print Spooler service via services.msc, which can resolve detection issues caused by a stuck spooler.
5. Update or reinstall the printer driver from the manufacturer's site or the internal Software Portal.
6. For USB printers, test a different USB cable and port, and confirm the printer is not in an error state (paper jam, low ink) that might block detection.
7. Escalate to L2/print services team if the printer remains undetected for this user while working for others on the network, or if it's an office-wide issue.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, network printers, USB printers
Category: Hardware / Printing

title: Print Jobs Stuck in Queue / Printer Not Printing
content:
Problem: A user sends a document to print, and the print job either gets stuck in the print queue indefinitely or the printer never produces the physical output.

Symptoms:
- Print job shows 'Printing' or 'Spooling' status in the queue but never completes
- Printer does not produce any output despite the job appearing to be sent successfully
- User reports 'my print job is stuck' or 'nothing is coming out of the printer'
- Queue may show an error status or simply remain unchanged for an extended period

Resolution Steps:
1. Open the print queue (double-click the printer icon in the system tray, or via Settings > Printers & scanners) and check the stuck job's status.
2. Cancel the stuck print job and attempt to print a fresh test page.
3. If the job will not cancel, restart the Print Spooler service via services.msc to force-clear the queue.
4. Check the physical printer for errors: paper jam, low toner/ink, out of paper, or an open cover/tray.
5. Confirm the printer is powered on, connected, and not in a sleep/power-save state that delays waking for jobs.
6. Restart both the printer and the laptop if the queue remains stuck after clearing it and restarting the spooler.
7. Escalate to L2/print services team if jobs consistently fail to print after spooler restart and printer status checks, especially if affecting multiple users on a shared printer.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, network printers, shared office printers
Category: Hardware / Printing

title: USB Device Not Recognized / 'Device Not Working Properly' Error
content:
Problem: A USB device (drive, peripheral, or accessory) connected to a laptop is not recognized by Windows, often accompanied by a 'USB Device Not Recognized' notification.

Symptoms:
- Notification reads 'USB Device Not Recognized' or 'The last USB device you connected to this computer malfunctioned'
- Device does not appear in File Explorer (for storage devices) or function in its intended application
- User reports 'my USB device isn't being recognized' or 'it says the device malfunctioned'
- Device may work correctly when tested in a different USB port or on a different computer

Resolution Steps:
1. Unplug the USB device and try a different USB port on the laptop, as a specific port may be at fault.
2. Test the device on a different computer to determine if the issue is with the device itself or the laptop.
3. Check Device Manager for the device listed under an error/unknown device category, and attempt to update its driver.
4. Uninstall the device from Device Manager (right-click > Uninstall device) and reconnect it to force Windows to reinstall the driver.
5. If using a USB hub, connect the device directly to the laptop instead to rule out a hub power or compatibility issue.
6. Check Device Manager > Universal Serial Bus controllers for any USB Root Hub showing an error, which may indicate a broader USB controller issue.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if the device remains unrecognized across multiple ports and after driver reinstall, as it may indicate a failing USB controller.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, USB devices, USB drives, USB peripherals
Category: Hardware / USB

title: Laptop Not Charging or Battery Draining Quickly
content:
Problem: A laptop either does not charge when plugged in, or the battery drains significantly faster than expected even under normal usage conditions.

Symptoms:
- Battery percentage does not increase, or decreases, while the charger is connected
- Charging indicator light on the laptop or charger does not illuminate as expected
- User reports 'my laptop won't charge' or 'the battery dies really fast now'
- Battery may drain to zero within an hour or two of unplugging, far below expected battery life

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the charger cable and adapter are fully and firmly connected at both the wall outlet and the laptop port.
2. Test with a different known-good charger/cable if available, to rule out a faulty charger.
3. Test a different power outlet to rule out an outlet-side power issue.
4. Check for visible damage to the charging cable or port (bent pins, frayed cable, loose port).
5. Check battery health/status in Windows via the built-in battery report (run 'powercfg /batteryreport' in Command Prompt) for a rapidly draining battery.
6. Update the laptop's BIOS/firmware and chipset drivers, as charging issues can sometimes stem from outdated power management firmware.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if the laptop does not charge with a confirmed-good charger and outlet, or if the battery report indicates significant capacity degradation, for a possible battery or charging port replacement.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, laptop batteries, laptop chargers
Category: Hardware / Power

title: Laptop Overheating / Fan Running Loudly
content:
Problem: A laptop becomes noticeably hot to the touch, and/or its internal fan runs at a loud, high speed continuously, even during relatively light usage.

Symptoms:
- Laptop chassis, particularly near the keyboard or underside, feels hot to the touch
- Fan noise is loud and constant, not just during demanding tasks
- User reports 'my laptop is overheating' or 'the fan is really loud all the time'
- Performance may also degrade (thermal throttling) alongside the heat and noise

Resolution Steps:
1. Check Task Manager for any process consuming unusually high CPU, as runaway processes are a common cause of excess heat and fan noise.
2. Ensure the laptop's ventilation areas (typically underside and side vents) are not blocked by soft surfaces (bed, couch cushions) or accumulated dust.
3. Close unnecessary applications and browser tabs to reduce processing load.
4. Check for pending Windows Updates or driver updates, as some updates address thermal management bugs.
5. Recommend the user use the laptop on a hard, flat surface to improve airflow rather than on soft surfaces.
6. Check the laptop's power plan settings; switching from a 'Best Performance' plan to 'Balanced' can reduce heat generation for non-demanding tasks.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if the laptop remains excessively hot or loud even at idle with minimal processes running, as it may indicate a failing fan or dust buildup requiring physical cleaning.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, all laptop hardware
Category: Hardware / Thermal

title: Bluetooth Device Won't Pair or Keeps Disconnecting
content:
Problem: A Bluetooth peripheral (headset, speaker, mouse, keyboard) either fails to pair with the laptop initially, or pairs successfully but disconnects repeatedly during use.

Symptoms:
- Device does not appear in the Bluetooth device scan, or pairing attempts time out or fail
- Previously paired device disconnects intermittently, requiring frequent reconnection
- User reports 'my Bluetooth device won't pair' or 'it keeps disconnecting'
- Device may pair and stay connected fine with a different computer or phone

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the device is charged (for battery-powered peripherals) and in pairing mode, typically indicated by a flashing status light.
2. Toggle Bluetooth off and on in Windows Settings to reset the adapter before attempting to pair again.
3. Remove the device from the paired devices list (Settings > Bluetooth & devices) if previously paired, then re-pair from scratch.
4. Move the device closer to the laptop and remove obstructions, as walls and distance can affect Bluetooth range/stability.
5. Update the laptop's Bluetooth driver via Device Manager.
6. Check for interference from other wireless devices (Wi-Fi routers, other Bluetooth peripherals) operating in close proximity.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the device model if pairing consistently fails or disconnects persist after re-pairing and driver updates.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, Bluetooth peripherals
Category: Hardware / Bluetooth

title: Docking Station or USB-C Hub Not Charging Laptop
content:
Problem: A laptop connected to a docking station or USB-C hub does not charge, or charges very slowly, even though the dock/hub is rated to provide sufficient power delivery.

Symptoms:
- Battery percentage does not increase, or increases very slowly, while connected to the dock/hub
- Laptop may show 'Not charging' or 'Slow charging' status near the battery icon
- User reports 'my laptop doesn't charge through the dock' or 'charging is really slow at my desk'
- Laptop charges normally when using its original charger directly

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the dock/hub is properly powered by its own power adapter (not solely relying on the laptop's USB-C connection), as many docks require external power to charge a connected laptop.
2. Check the wattage rating of the dock's power delivery versus the laptop's required charging wattage; underpowered docks will charge slowly or not at all under load.
3. Try a different USB-C cable if the cable is detachable, as low-quality or damaged cables can limit power delivery.
4. Test connecting the laptop's original charger directly to confirm the laptop itself charges normally outside the dock.
5. Update the dock's firmware via the manufacturer's utility, as firmware updates sometimes address power delivery negotiation issues.
6. Try a different port on the dock if multiple USB-C ports are available, as not all ports may support power delivery.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team with the dock model and laptop model if charging remains slow or absent after confirming adequate dock power rating and firmware updates.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, USB-C docking stations, USB-C hubs
Category: Hardware / Power

title: External Hard Drive or USB Storage Not Recognized
content:
Problem: An external hard drive or USB flash drive connected to a laptop does not appear in File Explorer, preventing the user from accessing or transferring files.

Symptoms:
- External drive does not appear in File Explorer under 'This PC' after connecting
- Drive's activity light may or may not illuminate when connected
- User reports 'my external drive isn't showing up' or 'I can't see my USB drive'
- Drive may be detected in Device Manager but not assigned a drive letter

Resolution Steps:
1. Try a different USB port on the laptop, as a specific port may not be providing adequate power or connectivity.
2. Test the drive on a different computer to determine if the issue is with the drive itself or the laptop.
3. Check Disk Management (right-click Start > Disk Management) to see if the drive is detected but simply lacks a drive letter or needs initialization.
4. If the drive appears in Disk Management without a letter, right-click the drive's volume and select 'Change Drive Letter and Paths' to assign one.
5. For drives requiring more power (some external HDDs), try a USB hub with its own power supply, or connect directly to the laptop rather than through an unpowered hub.
6. Check Device Manager for the drive listed under Disk drives with an error icon, and update the driver if present.
7. Escalate to L2/hardware team if the drive is not detected in Disk Management at all across multiple ports and computers, as it may indicate physical drive failure — advise the user not to attempt further troubleshooting if data recovery may be needed.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, external hard drives, USB flash drives
Category: Hardware / USB

title: Workday Portal Time-Off Submission Error and Session Timeout
content:
Problem: An employee in HR is unable to submit PTO or time-off requests in Workday, receiving a session timeout or submission processing error.

Symptoms:
- Workday displays 'Your session has expired' or 'Unable to process time-off request'
- Approvals and submitted leave requests fail to persist in the HR dashboard
- User reports 'I cannot submit my vacation days in Workday' or 'Workday times out on submission'
