- Affects HR team members managing PTO approvals and employee profile records

Resolution Steps:
1. Check browser cookies and cache for the Workday domain; clear cookies and restart browser session.
2. Verify the user is authenticated via corporate SSO/Okta and the session token has not expired.
3. Ensure pop-up blockers or aggressive ad-blockers are disabled for the corporate Workday tenant.
4. Verify that the employee direct reporting hierarchy and supervisory organization are active in Workday.
5. If submitting bulk approvals, test submitting single-record requests to isolate validation failures.
6. Check Workday system status for scheduled tenant maintenance or maintenance windows.
7. Escalate to HR Systems / Workday Operations with employee ID and screenshot of the error if session persists.

Affected Systems: Workday Cloud ERP, Chrome, Edge, HR Portal
Category: Applications / HR Systems

title: BambooHR Benefits Open Enrollment MFA Verification Failure
content:
Problem: HR personnel attempting to access employee benefits and open enrollment records in BambooHR are blocked by repeated MFA verification prompts or SMS token failure.

Symptoms:
- BambooHR login loops back to the MFA code prompt after entering valid credentials
- SMS verification token does not arrive or shows 'Code expired or invalid'
- User states 'BambooHR MFA is not sending codes' or 'I am locked out of benefits administration'
- Critical for open enrollment periods and benefits management

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the mobile device has active cellular reception and is not filtering automated 2FA shortcodes.
2. In the login portal, click 'Try another verification method' and select corporate Authenticator app (TOTP) or backup email.
3. Verify the time synchronization on the mobile device (Settings > Date and Time > Set Automatically) as time drift desynchronizes TOTP tokens.
4. Check if the HR user mobile phone number is correctly formatted with country code in BambooHR user settings.
5. Log into Okta/SSO first and launch BambooHR via the SSO chiclet rather than navigating directly to the URL.
6. Have an HR Admin reset the user BambooHR 2FA method if the registered device was replaced.
7. Escalate to Identity and Access Management (IAM) if directory sync from Entra ID to BambooHR has stalled.

Affected Systems: BambooHR, Okta SSO, Authenticator 2FA
Category: Access / HR

title: Salesforce CRM Single Sign-On Access Denied (Error: OAUTH_APP_ACCESS_DENIED)
content:
Problem: A sales representative or account executive cannot log into Salesforce Lightning CRM via corporate Single Sign-On, receiving error OAUTH_APP_ACCESS_DENIED or 'User does not have required profile assignment'.

Symptoms:
- Login redirection fails at corporate Okta/Azure SSO page
- Screen displays 'We cannot log you in because of an authentication error. (OAUTH_APP_ACCESS_DENIED)'
- User reports 'Salesforce will not let me sign in' or 'Salesforce says access denied'
- Blocks account management, lead pipeline tracking, and quota updating

Resolution Steps:
1. Confirm the sales representative has an active Salesforce license allocated in Okta/Entra ID User Assignments.
2. Verify the user is logging into the custom corporate domain (e.g., https://company.lightning.force.com) rather than standard login.salesforce.com.
3. Clear browser cache or try an incognito window to eliminate stale SAML/OAuth session cookies.
4. Check if the user recently transitioned roles or regions, which may have removed their Sales Profile assignment.
5. Verify that the user corporate email matches their Salesforce Federation ID exactly.
6. Check with Salesforce Admin whether IP restriction ranges or Login Hours policy on the user profile are blocking off-hours access.
7. Escalate to CRM Operations / Salesforce Admin team with the user email, Salesforce username, and exact error message.

Affected Systems: Salesforce Lightning, Okta SSO, Azure AD
Category: Applications / Sales CRM

title: HubSpot Sales Extension and Outlook Sync Disconnect
content:
Problem: The HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop or web add-in disconnects repeatedly, preventing email logging, deal tracking, and sequence automation for sales reps.

Symptoms:
- HubSpot add-in icon in Outlook appears greyed out or prompts 'Please log in to HubSpot' on every launch
- Track and Log checkboxes do not stay selected when composing emails
- User reports 'HubSpot will not track my emails in Outlook' or 'HubSpot keeps signing me out'
- Deal activities and meeting schedulers fail to sync to HubSpot CRM

Resolution Steps:
1. In Outlook, navigate to File > Manage Add-ins and confirm HubSpot Sales is enabled and not disabled for slow startup.
2. In HubSpot web app (Settings > General > Email), verify the connected inbox status shows 'Connected' with green indicator.
3. If disconnected in HubSpot settings, click Reconnect and authorize corporate Microsoft 365 permissions via OAuth.
4. Clear Outlook add-in cache: delete contents of %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Wef and restart Outlook.
5. If using Outlook on Windows, reinstall the HubSpot Sales for Windows tray app from official portal.
6. Verify user has third-party cookies enabled in default browser, as OAuth tokens require cross-domain cookies.
7. Escalate to RevOps / IT Productivity team if tenant-level M365 Mailbox permissions require re-consent.

Affected Systems: HubSpot CRM, Microsoft Outlook, Windows 10/11
Category: Software / Sales Productivity

title: Figma Enterprise Design Seat Revoked and Team Library Sync Conflict
content:
Problem: A product designer in UI/UX cannot edit team design files in Figma, showing 'View only' status or team library sync conflict errors.

Symptoms:
- User with previously granted editor permissions now sees 'View only' or 'Ask for edit access' banner
- Team shared design system components fail to publish or display 'Conflict while syncing library changes'
- User reports 'I cannot edit Figma files' or 'Figma says view only even though I am a designer'
- Blocks design handoff, sprint deliverables, and component updates

Resolution Steps:
1. Check the user Figma account email to ensure they are logged into the Enterprise Organization account, not a personal account.
2. In Figma Admin Console (or via manager approval), verify whether the user Design Seat was downgraded during monthly seat reclamation.
3. For library sync conflicts: duplicate the local component branch, pull latest library changes, and merge components manually.
4. Clear Figma desktop app cache: Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart.
5. If using Figma web, test in Chrome with hardware acceleration enabled (Settings > System > Use graphics acceleration).
6. If edit seat was reclaimed due to inactivity, submit an IT service request for 'Figma Enterprise Full Design Seat' with design lead approval.
7. Escalate to Design Operations / IT Software Procurement for immediate seat provisioning.

Affected Systems: Figma Desktop, Figma Web, macOS, Windows 11
Category: Applications / Design Tools

title: Adobe Creative Cloud Error 205 (License Verification and Asset Sync Failure)
content:
Problem: A UI/UX designer opening Photoshop, Illustrator, or After Effects is greeted with Error 205 or 'We were unable to verify your subscription status'.

Symptoms:
- Creative Cloud desktop app shows Error Code 205 or Error Code 206
- Design apps launch and immediately quit or switch to 7-day trial mode
- User reports 'Adobe says my license is expired or not verified' or 'Cannot open Illustrator'
- Creative Cloud Libraries fail to load cloud assets

Resolution Steps:
1. Ensure the user signs in with 'Company or School Account' (Federated ID / SSO) and NOT 'Personal Account'.
2. Close all Adobe applications and the Creative Cloud desktop app via Task Manager.
3. Open Windows Credential Manager (or macOS Keychain) and remove all credential entries containing 'Adobe App Info' or 'Adobe User'.
4. Relaunch Creative Cloud desktop app and sign in again through corporate Okta/Azure SSO.
5. Check the host file (C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts) to ensure no Adobe activation domains are blocked.
6. If Error 205 persists, run the official Adobe Limited Access Repair Tool to restore secure HTTPS connectivity to Adobe licensing servers.
7. Escalate to IT Asset Management if the corporate Adobe Enterprise Named User license has expired or needs re-allocation.

Affected Systems: Adobe Creative Cloud, Photoshop, Illustrator, Windows 11, macOS
Category: Software / Creative Applications

title: Greenhouse ATS Candidate Offer Letter E-Sign Integration Failure
content:
Problem: A recruiter in Talent Acquisition cannot generate or send candidate offer letters through Greenhouse ATS due to e-signature (DocuSign/HelloSign) API integration failure.

Symptoms:
- Clicking 'Generate Offer Letter' results in 'Error generating document: Integration error 500'
- E-signature status shows 'Pending sync' indefinitely and candidate does not receive signature request
- User reports 'Greenhouse will not send the offer letter' or 'DocuSign offer letter failed in Greenhouse'
- High urgency issue impacting candidate closing and hiring deadlines

Resolution Steps:
1. Verify the offer template fields in Greenhouse: ensure all required custom tokens (Salary, Start Date, Title) are filled in candidate profile.
2. In Greenhouse > Configure > Dev Center > Integrations, check the status of the DocuSign/HelloSign integration.
3. If integration token expired, have a Greenhouse Site Admin re-authenticate the e-signature service account.
4. Check candidate email address for special characters or invalid spaces that reject document delivery.
5. Test downloading the offer letter as PDF directly from Greenhouse to verify document merge formatting.
6. Check DocuSign/HelloSign service status dashboard for active API outages.
7. Escalate immediately to TA Systems Specialist or L2 Helpdesk as High Priority to manually dispatch offer if deadline is imminent.

Affected Systems: Greenhouse ATS, DocuSign API, Talent Acquisition
Category: Applications / Recruiting

title: LinkedIn Recruiter Seat Token Expiration and InMail Sync Error
content:
Problem: A recruiter in Talent Acquisition cannot search candidates or send InMails in LinkedIn Recruiter, receiving token expiration or 403 Forbidden errors.

Symptoms:
- LinkedIn Recruiter displays 'Your LinkedIn Recruiter seat session has expired' or prompts for personal password repeatedly
- InMail messages fail to send or do not log to Greenhouse ATS integration
- User reports 'Cannot message candidates on LinkedIn Recruiter' or 'Recruiter seat disconnected'
- Affects active hiring pipelines and candidate outreach

Resolution Steps:
1. Log out of LinkedIn.com completely, clear browser cookies for linkedin.com, and log back in using corporate email.
2. Access LinkedIn Recruiter via the corporate direct link (https://www.linkedin.com/talent/home) rather than the standard public feed.
3. Check if corporate SSO authentication is enforced: re-authenticate via company Okta/Azure SSO portal.
4. In LinkedIn Account Settings, verify that the recruiter contract profile is mapped to the active corporate seat license.
5. If Greenhouse integration is disconnected, navigate to LinkedIn Recruiter > Integrations > ATS and toggle sync.
6. Verify with TA Lead whether user Recruiter seat was reassigned or pooled during recruiter seat rotation.
7. Escalate to TA Operations / IT Software Licensing for LinkedIn seat re-provisioning.

Affected Systems: LinkedIn Recruiter, Chrome, Greenhouse Sync
Category: Applications / Recruiting

title: Docker Desktop WSL2 Backend Kernel Crash and VHDX Corruption
content:
Problem: A software engineer on Windows 11 cannot start Docker Desktop, receiving error 'Docker Desktop - Unexpected WSL error' or 'wsl.exe exited with code 4294967295'.

Symptoms:
- Docker Desktop whale icon in system tray remains red or in 'Docker Desktop is starting...' loop
- Command line 'docker ps' returns 'error during connect: This error may indicate that the docker daemon is not running'
- User reports 'Docker will not start on Windows' or 'WSL2 kernel error in Docker'
- Blocks local service compilation, containerized dev environments, and integration tests

Resolution Steps:
1. Open PowerShell as Administrator and run: wsl --status to inspect default WSL2 version and kernel version.
2. Run: wsl --update to ensure the WSL2 Linux kernel package is fully updated to latest release.
3. Shut down all WSL instances cleanly: wsl --shutdown, wait 10 seconds, then restart Docker Desktop.
4. Check free space on C: drive: WSL2 ext4.vhdx disk image requires at least 25 GB free to expand.
5. If docker-desktop-data VHDX is corrupt, run Docker Desktop > Troubleshoot (bug icon) > 'Clean / Purge data'.
6. Verify Hyper-V and Virtual Machine Platform are enabled in Windows Features.
7. Escalate to Senior Engineering IT / DevOps if nested virtualization or corporate endpoint antivirus is blocking WSL hypervisor calls.

Affected Systems: Docker Desktop, Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2), Windows 11
Category: Engineering / Development Tools

title: AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO) CLI Token Expiration and AssumeRole Denied
content:
Problem: An engineer running AWS CLI commands receives 'The security token included in the request is expired' or 'AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole'.

Symptoms:
- Terminal commands like 'aws s3 ls' or 'terraform plan' fail with ExpiredToken or AccessDenied
- Local ~/.aws/sso/cache tokens have exceeded their 8-hour maximum session duration
- User reports 'AWS CLI says token expired' or 'Terraform cannot authenticate to AWS'
- Blocks deployment pipelines, cloud infrastructure provisioning, and service debugging

Resolution Steps:
1. In terminal, run: aws sso login --profile <profile_name> to initiate an SSO authentication flow in browser.
2. Complete the corporate Okta/Azure AD authentication and approve the authorization code in browser.
3. Verify your active AWS role and account: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile <profile_name>.
4. If using environment variables, ensure AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_SESSION_TOKEN in terminal do not override SSO config.
5. If token cache is corrupted, delete files in ~/.aws/sso/cache/ and re-run aws sso login.
6. If AccessDenied persists after successful login, verify in AWS SSO portal whether user has been added to required AWS Permission Set.
7. Escalate to Cloud Platform / DevOps team with user ARN and target AWS Account ID if role assignment is missing.

Affected Systems: AWS CLI, AWS IAM Identity Center, Terraform, macOS/Linux/Windows
Category: Engineering / Cloud Infrastructure

title: GitHub Enterprise SSH Key Authentication Denied (Permission Denied publickey)
content:
Problem: A developer running 'git push' or 'git clone' against GitHub Enterprise is rejected with error 'Permission denied (publickey). fatal: Could not read from remote repository.'

Symptoms:
- Git operations over SSH fail with 'git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)'
- SSH test command 'ssh -T git@github.com' fails or reports incorrect username
- User reports 'GitHub rejected my SSH key' or 'Cannot push code to GitHub'
- Developer was recently onboarded or switched machines

Resolution Steps:
1. Verify SSH agent is running: eval $(ssh-agent -s) and list loaded keys with: ssh-add -l.
2. If no keys listed, load your private key: ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 (or id_rsa).
3. Check public key on GitHub: cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub and verify it is registered under GitHub Settings > SSH and GPG keys.
4. Crucial: Ensure the SSH key is authorized for the corporate GitHub Enterprise Organization (click 'Configure SSO' next to the key).
5. Check SSH config file (~/.ssh/config) to ensure Host github.com specifies IdentityFile and User git correctly.
6. Test connectivity with verbose output: ssh -vT git@github.com to identify rejected cipher or missing key.
7. Escalate to Engineering Ops / DevTools team if GitHub Enterprise organization SAML authorization fails to link to the key.

Affected Systems: Git, GitHub Enterprise, SSH, macOS, Linux, Windows 11
Category: Engineering / Version Control

title: Kubernetes kubectl TLS Certificate Expired on Staging Cluster
content:
Problem: An engineer running 'kubectl get pods' or deploying manifests receives 'Unable to connect to the server: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid'.

Symptoms:
- All kubectl commands to staging or dev cluster fail with x509 certificate error
- Helm charts and k9s fail to connect to the Kubernetes API server
- User reports 'kubectl certificate expired' or 'Cannot connect to Kubernetes cluster'
- Blocks engineering deployments and microservice logs inspection

Resolution Steps:
1. Check current kubeconfig context: kubectl config current-context.
2. Update local cluster credentials using cloud provider CLI:
   - For EKS: aws eks update-kubeconfig --region <region> --name <cluster_name>
   - For GKE: gcloud container clusters get-credentials <cluster_name> --region <region>
   - For AKS: az aks get-credentials --resource-group <rg> --name <cluster_name> --overwrite-existing
3. Verify your local system clock is accurate (Settings > Date and Time > Sync Now), as clock skew triggers false x509 expiration errors.
4. Clear cached client certificates in ~/.kube/cache and inspect ~/.kube/config for expired client-certificate-data.
5. If API server itself has expired control plane certs (e.g. kubeadm cluster), notify DevOps/Platform team immediately.
6. Test connectivity with: kubectl version --short.
7. Escalate to Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) / Kubernetes Platform team if cluster-side certificate renewal is required.

Affected Systems: Kubernetes, kubectl, EKS, GKE, AKS, Linux, macOS, Windows
Category: Engineering / Kubernetes
